Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 4:

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses — lash them with eighty lashes﴾. By "casting" (ramy) He means accusing (qadhf) of fornication (zina). Whoever accuses a muhsan or muhsanah (a free, chaste person of good standing) of fornication, saying to them, "You committed zina" or "O fornicator," is obligated to receive eighty lashes if he is free. If he is a slave, he is lashed forty. If the one accused is not muhsan, the accuser incurs ta'zir (discretionary punishment).

The conditions of ihsan (the state of being muhsan, i.e., eligible for this protection) are five: Islam, sanity, puberty, freedom, and chastity from fornication. So if a person committed fornication once in the early part of his puberty, then repented, his condition became good, and his life was prolonged, and then an accuser accused him, there is no hadd (prescribed punishment) against the accuser. If the accused person confesses to fornication against himself, or the accuser produces four witnesses to his fornication, the hadd falls from the accuser, because the hadd that was due upon him is the hadd of slander (al-fiyah), and its truthfulness has been established.

As for His statement, ﴿and those who cast accusations against chaste women﴾, meaning: those who accuse chaste women of fornication, namely the Muslim, free, chaste women; ﴿then do not produce four witnesses﴾ who testify to their fornication; ﴿lash them with eighty lashes﴾, meaning: strike them with eighty lashes.

﴿And never accept their testimony thereafter, and those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 5–6:

﴿Except for those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the acceptance of the testimony of the one who commits slander (qadhf, falsely accusing someone of unchastity) after repentance, and regarding the ruling of this exception. A group held that the testimony of the slanderer is rejected because of the act of slander itself, and that if he repents, regrets what he said, and his condition becomes good, his testimony is accepted, whether he repents after the prescribed punishment (hadd, the fixed penalty) has been carried out on him or before it. Their evidence is the words of the Exalted: ﴿except for those who repent﴾. They said: the exception refers to both the testimony and the wickedness, so after repentance his testimony is accepted and the name of wickedness is removed from him. This is reported from Ibn Abbas and Umar, and it is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata', Tawus, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sulayman ibn Yasar, al-Sha'bi, Ikrimah, Umar ibn Abd al-'Aziz and al-Zuhri. Malik and al-Shafi'i also held this view.

Another group held that the testimony of one who has been punished for slander is never accepted, even if he repents. They said: the exception refers to His words: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient﴾. This is the view of al-Nakha'i, Shurayh and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y). They said: his testimony is not rejected because of the slander itself as long as he has not been punished.

Al-Shafi'i said: "He is worse before he is punished than when he is punished, because the hudud are expiations. So how can they reject him in his better state and accept him in his worse state?" Al-Sha'bi held that the hadd for slander falls away through repentance, and he said: the exception refers to everything.

The general body of scholars hold that it does not fall away through repentance, except that if the one slandered pardons him, it falls away. This is like retaliation (qisas), which falls away through pardon, but does not fall away through repentance.

If it is said: "If you accept his testimony after repentance, then what is the meaning of His words ﴿ever﴾?"

It is said: its meaning is that his testimony is not accepted ever, as long as he persists in his slander, because the "ever" of each person is his lifetime according to his state, just as one says: "The testimony of the disbeliever is never accepted," meaning as long as he remains a disbeliever. [[See a detailed explanation of these opinions with their weighing (tarjih) in al-Tabari: 18/76–81.]]

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, that is, who slander their women, ﴿and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ who testify to the truth of what they said, ﴿except themselves﴾, that is, other than themselves, ﴿then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "arba'u shahadat" with the ayn in the nominative (raf'), as the predicate of the subject, meaning: then the testimony of one of them, which averts the punishment, is four testimonies. The others read it in the accusative (nasb), meaning: then the testimony of one of them is that he testifies four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 7 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿And the fifth (testimony) is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars.﴾ Nafi' and Ya'qub read *anna* (أَنْ) with a light (non-emphatic) *nun*, and likewise the second, *la'nat Allah* (لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ) is in the nominative. Then Ya'qub read *ghadab* (غَضَبُ) in the nominative, while Nafi' read *ghadiba* (غَضِبَ) with a kasra on the *dad* and a fatha on the *ba'*, as a past verb, with *Allah* (اللَّهُ) in the nominative. The others read *anna* (أَنَّ) with the emphatic *shaddah* in both places, *la'nata* (لعنة) in the accusative, and *ghadaba* (غضب) with a fatha on the *dad* as a noun, with *Allah* (اللَّهِ) in the genitive. Hafs, from 'Asim, read *wal-khamisata* (وَالْخَامِسَةَ) with the second word in the accusative, meaning: and he shall testify the fifth testimony. The others read it in the nominative, as the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is in *anna*, like the first.

The occasion of revelation of this verse is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, that Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi informed him that 'Uwaymir al-'Ajlani came to 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari and said to him: "O 'Asim, what do you think if a man finds another man with his wife; will he kill him, and will you kill him? Or how should he act? Ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this for me, O 'Asim." He said: So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked the questions and found fault with them, until what 'Asim heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) weighed heavily on him. When 'Asim returned to his family, 'Uwaymir came to him and said: "O 'Asim, what did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say to you?" 'Asim said to 'Uwaymir: "You have brought me no good. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked the question you asked him about." 'Uwaymir said: "By Allah, I will not stop until I ask him about it." So 'Uwaymir came while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in the midst of the people, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds another man with his wife; will he kill him, and will you kill him? Or how should he act?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, it has been revealed concerning you and your wife. Go and bring her." Sahl said: "So they performed *li'an* (mutual imprecation) while I was with the people in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When they finished their mutual imprecation, 'Uwaymir said: 'I have lied against her, O Messenger of Allah, if I keep her,' and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to do so." Malik said: Ibn Shihab said: "That became the sunnah of the two who perform *li'an*."[[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', chapter on what has come concerning *li'an*, no. 34: 2/566-567; and by al-Bukhari in *Talaq*, chapter: *li'an* and whoever divorces after *li'an*: 9/446, and in other places; and by Muslim at the beginning of the chapter on *li'an*, no. 1492: 2/1129-1130; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/250.]]

Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: Ishaq informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, al-Awza'i informed us, al-Zuhri informed us with this chain of narration, with a similar meaning, and he added: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Look at her: if she gives birth to a child with black hair, large dark eyes, large buttocks, and thick calves, then I do not think 'Uwaymir has told the truth about her." And if she gives birth to one who is reddish, like [...] [[It has become well known in the books of usul with this wording what Ibn Majah narrated in the book of divorce, chapter on the divorce of one under compulsion or forgetful, through the route of al-Walid ibn Muslim from al-Awza'i from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas, with the wording: "Indeed Allah has removed from my community error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." All its narrators are trustworthy, but there is a break (inqita') between Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata'. Al-Busiri pointed to this in al-Zawa'id, saying: its chain is sound if the break is set aside, and it has been transmitted with other wordings which strengthen one another. See Irwa' al-Ghalil of Shaykh al-Albani 1/123, al-Mu'tabar fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Minhaj, and al-Mukhtasar of al-Zarkashi p. 154.]] then I do not think 'Uwaymir has lied about her." She gave birth to the child in the description which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had stated, confirming 'Uwaymir. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *Talaq*, chapter: the mutual imprecation in the mosque: 9/452-453; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/252.]] Afterwards he was called by his mother's name.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar informed us, Ibn Abi 'Adi informed us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, Ikrima informed us, from Ibn 'Abbas, that Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife before the Prophet (ﷺ) of [adultery] with Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Produce evidence, or the hadd punishment will be on your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man upon his wife, must he go searching for evidence?" The Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying: "Evidence, or else the hadd punishment on your back." Hilal said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I am truthful, and Allah will surely reveal something that will clear my back from the hadd." Then Jibril descended and revealed to him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ He recited until he reached ﴿...if he is among the truthful.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) departed and sent for them both. Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was saying: "Indeed Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will either of you repent?" Then she stood and testified. When she reached the fifth, they stopped her and said: "Indeed it is binding (mujibah)." Ibn 'Abbas said: She hesitated and drew back until we thought she would retract. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day," and she went on. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Watch her: if she gives birth to one with very black eyes,[[intensely black.]] with full buttocks,[[complete and large buttocks.]] with thick calves,[[large.]] then he belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'." She gave birth to him in that manner. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not for what has passed from the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary of Surah al-Nur, chapter: "and she shall avert the punishment by testifying four times by Allah that he is surely among the liars": 8/449, and in other places; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/259-260.]]

Ikrima narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: He said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women...﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubada said: "If I came upon a woman with a man between her thighs, I would not disturb him until I brought four witnesses. By Allah, I would not bring four witnesses before he had finished his need and left. And if I said what I saw, there would be eighty lashes on my back." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief has said?" They said: "Do not blame him, for he is a man of jealousy; he never married a woman except a virgin, and he never divorced a woman he had, so that any man of us dared to marry her." Sa'd said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, by Allah I know that it is from Allah, and that it is the truth, but I was astonished by it when I told you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah refuses anything but that." Sa'd said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth." He said: They did not remain long before Hilal ibn Umayya, a paternal cousin of his, came from his garden. He saw a man with his wife, committing adultery with her, so he held back until morning. When morning came, he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was sitting with his companions, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with my wife. I saw it with my own eyes and heard it with my own ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought him, and it weighed heavily on him, until that was recognized in his face. Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I see the aversion in your face at what I have brought you. Allah knows that I am truthful and I have said nothing but the truth, and I hope that Allah will grant me a way out." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to strike him. The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Sa'd said: Hilal will be lashed and his testimony annulled." While they were in this state, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wanted to order that he be struck, revelation descended upon him. His companions fell silent so as not to speak to him, when they knew that revelation had come down to him, until he finished. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ up to the end of the verses. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made a way out for you." He said: "I had been hoping for that from Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her." She came, and when the two of them were gathered before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), she was asked, and she denied it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will either of you repent?" Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, I have spoken the truth and said nothing but the truth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perform *li'an* between them." It was said to Hilal: "Testify." He testified four times by Allah that he is surely among the truthful. He said to him at the fifth: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter, and Allah's punishment is more severe than the punishment of people, and this fifth is the binding one which makes the punishment obligatory upon you." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flog me for it." He testified the fifth: "That the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars." Then he said to the woman: "Testify." She testified four times by Allah that he is surely among the liars. He said to her at the fifth, and stopped her: "Fear Allah, for the fifth is binding, and Allah's punishment is more severe than the punishment of people." She hesitated for a while and was inclined to confess, then she said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people," and she testified the fifth: "That the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then separated them, and ruled that the child belongs to the mother, and that he is not to be called after a father, nor is his mother to be accused. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If she gives birth to him in such and such a way, then he belongs to her husband; and if she gives birth to him in such and such a way, then he belongs to the one who was accused." She gave birth to him as a boy like a dark-reddish camel,[[Translator's note: the Arabic *awraq* denotes a dusky, greyish-brown colour.]] resembling the hated likeness. He later became governor of Egypt, not knowing who his father was.[[Narrated by Muslim in *li'an*, no. 1498: 2/1135; and the author narrated part of it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/265.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said, in the other narrations, and Muqatil said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it on Friday from the pulpit. 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari stood up and said: "May Allah make me your ransom. If one of us sees a man with his wife and tells of what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes, the Muslims call him a wicked person (fasiq), and his testimony is never accepted. So how can we find witnesses? When we look for witnesses, the man will have finished his need and gone away." 'Asim had a paternal cousin called Uwaymir, whose wife was called Khawlah bint Qays ibn Muhsan. Uwaymir came to 'Asim and said: "I saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' on the belly of my wife Khawlah." 'Asim said "Inna lillah" (we belong to Allah) [35/b] and went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the following Friday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how quickly I have been tested with the question you were asked last Friday, concerning my own household." He told him. Uwaymir, Khawlah and Shurayk were all paternal cousins of 'Asim. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them all and said to Uwaymir: "Fear Allah concerning your wife and your cousin, and do not accuse her of slander." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I swear by Allah that I saw Shurayk on her belly. I have not approached her for four months, and she is pregnant by someone other than me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the woman: "Fear Allah, and say nothing except what you have done." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, Uwaymir is a jealous man. He saw me and Shurayk talking together at length in the evening, and jealousy drove him to what he said." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Shurayk: "What do you say?" He said: "What the woman says is a lie." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that the call "As-salatu jami'ah" (prayer is about to be gathered) be made. He led the 'Asr prayer, then said to Uwaymir: "Stand up." He stood and said: "I testify by Allah that Khawlah is an adulteress, and that I am truly among the truthful." Then in the second oath he said: "I testify that I saw Shurayk on her belly, and that I am truly among the truthful." In the third he said: "I testify by Allah that she is pregnant by someone other than me, and that I am truly among the truthful." In the fourth he said: "I testify by Allah that I have not approached her for four months, and that I am truly among the truthful." In the fifth he said: "The curse of Allah be upon Uwaymir (meaning himself) if he is among the liars concerning what he has said." Then he ordered him to sit down and said to Khawlah: "Stand up." She stood and said: "I testify by Allah that I am not an adulteress, and that Uwaymir is among the liars." Then in the second she said: "I testify by Allah that he did not see Shurayk on my belly, and that he is among the liars." In the third she said: "I testify by Allah that he is the father of the child I am carrying, and that he is among the liars." In the fourth she said: "I testify by Allah that he never saw me in an act of immorality, and that he is among the liars." In the fifth she said: "The anger of Allah be upon Khawlah (meaning herself) if he is among the truthful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then separated them, and said: "Were it not for these oaths, I would have had an opinion on their affair." Then he said: "Watch for her delivery. If she brings forth a child [with reddish hair (usaybih)][[al-Usaybih: diminutive of al-Ashhab, the one with a reddish tint, like a light red colour. In manuscript "A" it reads "bi-ashhab" instead of "bihi usaybih".]] [short-bodied with a prominent back (uthaybij)][[al-Uthaybij: diminutive of al-Athbaj, the one with a protruding back. The thabaj is the area between the shoulder blades and the middle of the back. In manuscript "A" the phrase reads "aslah asahb".]] and it is dark-coloured, then he belongs to Shurayk. If she brings forth one who is ashen-grey (awraq), with frizzy hair (ja'd), with large limbs like a camel (jamali), with thick calves (khadlaj al-saqayn), then he belongs to the one she was accused with." Ibn 'Abbas said: "She brought forth the child most resembling Shurayk among all of Allah's creation."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in abridged form: 18/84.]]

As for the ruling of the verse: when a man accuses his wife of adultery, the consequence is the same as the consequence of accusing a stranger, namely that he is liable to the prescribed punishment (hadd) if she is chaste (muhsanah), or to discretionary punishment (ta'zir) if she is not chaste. However, the way out of these two is different. If he accuses a stranger, the hadd is imposed on him, unless he produces four witnesses to his adultery, or the accused admits it, in which case the hadd for slander falls from him. In the case of a wife, if he finds one of these two (witnesses or confession), or performs li'an (mutual oaths of cursing), the hadd falls from him. Thus li'an in the case of accusing a wife is in place of evidence, because a man who sees a man with his wife may be unable to establish evidence against him, and cannot bear the shame. So Allah made li'an a proof in his favour regarding his truthfulness. He, Exalted, said: ﴿So the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the truthful﴾. If the husband produces evidence of her adultery, or she confesses to adultery, the hadd and li'an fall from him, except where there is a child whom he wishes to disown; then he may perform li'an to deny paternity.

When the ruler (imam) wishes to conduct li'an between them, he begins by having the man stand, and instructs him in the words of li'an. He says: "Say: I testify by Allah that I am surely among the truthful regarding what I have accused so-and-so of, namely adultery." If he accused her of a specific man, he names him by name in the li'an; if he accused her of a group, he names them. The husband repeats after the ruler as he is instructed. If there is a child or a foetus whom he wishes to disown, he says: "And this child or foetus is of adultery; it is not from me." In the fifth oath he says: "The curse of Allah be upon me if I am among the liars regarding what I have accused so-and-so of." If he utters any of these words without the judge's instruction, it is not counted. When the man has finished the li'an, separation occurs between him and his wife, and she becomes forbidden to him permanently. Paternity is negated from him, and the hadd for slander falls from him. The woman becomes liable to the hadd for adultery: if she is chaste (muhsanah), she is stoned; if she is not chaste, she is flogged and exiled. These are five rulings, all of which relate to the husband's li'an.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 8–9:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿wayadra'u﴾ (yadfa'u, "and it averts"), ﴿'anha al-'adhaba an tashhada arba'a shahadatin billahi innahu lamina al-kadhibin﴾ ("the punishment from her, that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars"), ﴿wal-khamisata anna ghadaba Allahi 'alayha in kana mina al-sadiqin﴾ ("and the fifth, that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful").

He meant by "the punishment" the legal penalty (hadd), as He said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿wal-yashhad 'adhabahuma ta'ifatun mina al-mu'minin﴾ ("and let a group of the believers witness their punishment"), meaning their legal penalty.

The meaning of the verse is: when the husband performs li'an, the wife becomes liable to the legal penalty for adultery (hadd al-zina). When the legal penalty for adultery has become due upon her through his li'an, and she wishes to remove it from herself, then she performs li'an: she stands and, after the judge admonishes her, testifies four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars regarding what he has accused me of, and in the fifth she says: "upon me be the wrath of Allah if my husband is among the truthful regarding what he has accused me of."

Only one ruling is attached to her li'an, namely the removal of the legal penalty from her. If the husband establishes evidence of her adultery, the penalty is not removed from her by li'an.

According to the companions of opinion (ashab al-ra'y, the Hanafis): there is no legal penalty upon one who slanders his wife; rather its requirement is li'an. If he does not perform li'an, he is imprisoned until he performs it. When the husband has performed li'an but the wife refuses to perform li'an, she is imprisoned until she performs it.

According to others: li'an is a proof of his truthfulness, and the one who slanders, if he refrains from establishing proof of his truthfulness, is not imprisoned but is subjected to the legal penalty, like one who slanders a stranger when he refrains from establishing evidence.

According to Abu Hanifa: the requirement of li'an is the occurrence of separation (furqa) and the negation of paternity (nafy al-nasab), and these two occur only through the li'an of both spouses together and the ruling of the judge.

The separation by li'an, according to many scholars of knowledge, is a separation by annulment (faskh), and this is the view of al-Shafi'i. That separation is perpetual, so that even if the husband denies himself, that is accepted regarding what is against him but not regarding what is in his favour: he becomes liable to the legal penalty and the child is attributed to him, but the perpetual prohibition of marriage is not lifted.

According to Abu Hanifa, the separation by li'an is a separation by divorce (talaq). So if the husband denies himself, it is permissible for him to marry her again. If he utters only some of the words of li'an, the ruling is not attached to it. According to Abu Hanifa, if he utters most of the words of li'an, it stands in place of all of them regarding the attachment of the ruling to it.

Everyone whose oath is valid, his li'an is valid, whether free or slave, Muslim or dhimmi. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sulayman ibn Yasar and al-Hasan, and Rabi'a, Malik, al-Thawri, al-Shafi'i and most scholars held it. Al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i and the companions of opinion said: li'an applies only between two free Muslims who are not subject to the legal penalty; if the spouses, or one of them, is a slave, or a dhimmi, or has been subjected to the legal penalty for slander, then there is no li'an between them.

The apparent meaning of the Qur'an is a proof for the one who said that li'an applies between them, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿wal-ladhina yarmuna azwajahum﴾ ("and those who accuse their wives"), and He did not distinguish between free and slave, or the one subject to the legal penalty and others, as He said: ﴿alladhina yuzahiruna min nisa'ihim﴾ (Al-Mujadila: 2) ("those of you who divorce by zihar from their wives"). Then free and slave are equal here in zihar. And li'an is not valid except before the judge or his deputy.

Li'an is made more severe by four things: by the number of the formulas, by the place, by the time, and that it be in the presence of a group of people. As for the prescribed formulas, it is not permissible to omit any of them. As for the place, it is that he performs li'an in the most noble of places: if it is in Makkah, then between the Corner (al-Rukn) and the Station (al-Maqam); if it is in Madinah, then at the minbar; and in the rest of the lands, in the congregational mosque at the minbar. The time is after the 'asr prayer. As for the gathering, its minimum is four persons. The making more severe by a gathering is recommended, so that even if the judge performs li'an between them alone, it is permissible [[omitted in manuscript "a"]]. Whether making more severe by place and time is obligatory or recommended, there are two opinions.

The Qur'anic verse: "Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise."

His words: ﴿And had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Oft-Returning (tawwab), All-Wise (hakim)﴾. The answer to "law la" (had it not been) is omitted. The meaning is: He would have hastened punishment upon you, but He concealed (your sin) and averted the prescribed penalty (hadd) from you through li'an (mutual imprecation). "Indeed Allah is Oft-Returning" means He turns back in mercy toward whoever turns away from acts of disobedience. "All-Wise" means in what He has ordained of prescribed punishments.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 11 (part 1 of 2)

His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a band among you﴾ and the verses that follow. The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse is what was reported to us by Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd Allah informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Alqamah ibn Waqqas and Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud narrated to me, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the People of the Slander (ahl al-ifk) said what they said about her. Each of them narrated to me a portion of her account, and some of them had a better memory of her narration than others and a more precise recounting of it. I have retained from each man of them the narration that he related to me from Aishah, and some of their narrations confirm others.

They said: Aishah said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever of them the lot fell upon, the Prophet (ﷺ) would take her with him." Aishah said: "He drew lots among us in a military expedition (ghazwah) he undertook, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after the veil (hijab) had been revealed. I used to be carried in a howdah (hawdaj) and I would dismount within it. We journeyed on until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished that expedition, then he turned back, and as we drew near to Medina on our return, he announced the departure one night. I stood up when they announced the departure and walked until I passed beyond the army. When I had finished my need, I came back to my riding-place (rahl), and I felt my chest, and behold, my necklace of Zifar onyx [[jaz': a known stone with black and white veins like roots; Ibn al-Qatta' said it is a singular noun with no plural, while Ibn Sayyidah said it is the plural of jaz'ah, and it is with a fatha.]] had broken. So I returned and searched for my necklace, and my searching for it detained me." She said: "The men who used to load my howdah came and lifted it and placed it upon my camel, the one I used to ride, and they thought I was inside it. At that time women were light and did not grow heavy, and they did not eat much meat; they only ate a little food [[al-'ulqah: what one subsists upon of provisions.]]. So the people did not notice the lightness of the howdah when they lifted and carried it. I was a young girl of tender age. They made the camel rise and set off, and I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their resting-places, and there was no one there, neither caller nor answerer. So I went to my place where I had been, thinking that they would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me and I slept.

Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, was behind the army. He arrived at my place in the morning and saw the shape of a sleeping person, and he recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the veil was revealed. I awoke at his saying the words 'Inna lillah wa inna ilayhi raji'un' when he recognized me. I covered my face with my outer garment (jilbab). By Allah, we exchanged no word, and I heard from him no word other than his saying 'Inna lillah.' He lowered himself until he made his mount kneel, and he stepped on its forelegs, and I got up to it and mounted it. He set off leading the mount by the reins until we reached the army at the height of midday, while they were resting."

She said: "So those who perished, perished. The one who took upon himself the greatest part of the slander was Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul." Urwah said: "I was told that it was spread about and talked of in his presence, and he would approve of it, listen to it, and spread it further."

Urwah also said: "Of the People of the Slander, only Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah and Hamnah bint Jahsh were named, along with other people whom I do not know, except that they were a band, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the one who took upon himself the greatest part of it﴾ — he said: Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul." Urwah said: "Aishah used to dislike that Hassan be insulted in her presence, and she would say: 'It was he who said: Indeed my father, my mother and my honour are a shield for the honour of Muhammad from among you.'"

Aishah said: "We arrived in Medina, and I fell ill when I arrived, for a month, while the people were deeply engaged in the talk of the People of the Slander, and I was unaware of any of it. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not recognize from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would only come in to me, greet, then say, 'How are you?' and then depart. That troubled me, and I was unaware of the evil. Then I went out once I had recovered, going out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi', which was our place for relieving ourselves, and we did not go out except at night to night. That was before we took latrines close to our houses, and our custom was the custom of the early Arabs regarding relieving themselves in the open toward the wilderness; we found the latrines near our houses troublesome."

She said: "I set out, I and Umm Mistah, who is the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. Umm Mistah and I turned back toward my house when we had finished our business. Umm Mistah stumbled in her cloak and said, 'May Mistah perish!' I said to her: 'What a bad thing you said! Will you curse a man who witnessed Badr?' She said: 'O you (ay hentah) [[ay: a particle of calling for the distant, and it may be used for the near when they are treated as distant; hentah: with a fatha on the ha and a sukun on the nun, and it may be followed by a taa with a fatha, ending in a silent ha, and it may be pronounced with a damma; it is said it means "this one", and it is said it means "you are unaware", as though she were attributing to her little knowledge of the people's schemes.]], have you not heard what he said?' I said: 'What did he say?' So she told me the talk of the People of the Slander. She said: 'My sickness increased upon my sickness.' When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me, then said, 'How are you?' I said to him: 'Will you permit me to go to my parents?' She said: 'I wanted to ascertain the news from their side.' She said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me permission. I said to my mother: "O mother, what are people talking about?"' She said: 'O daughter, calm yourself, for by Allah, rarely has there been a woman who was beloved by a husband who loved her and had co-wives, without them increasing talk about her.' I said: 'Glory be to Allah! Have people truly talked about this?' She said: 'So I wept that night until morning, my tears not ceasing and I not sleeping at all. Then I awoke weeping.'"

She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, asking them and consulting them about parting from his family. As for Usamah, he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with what he knew of the innocence of his family and with what he knew of his feelings toward them. Usamah said: 'Keep your wife, for we know nothing but good.' As for Ali, he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women other than her. Ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth.'" She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Barirah and said: 'O Barirah, have you seen anything that makes you doubt?' Barirah said to him: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I have never seen anything in her that I would overlook, except that she is a young girl of tender age, who sleeps and neglects her family's dough, so a domestic goat comes and eats it.'"

She said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up that same day and asked for Abd Allah ibn Ubayy to be excused while he was on the pulpit, and said: 'O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm toward my family has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing of my family but good, and they have mentioned a man of whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my house except with me.'" She said: "Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, stood up and said: 'I, O Messenger of Allah, will excuse you. If he is from the Aws, I will strike off his neck, and if he is from our brothers of the Khazraj, command us and we will do your command.'" She said: "A man of the Khazraj stood up, and he was a cousin of Hassan's mother from his clan, and he was Sa'd ibn Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj. She said: 'Before that he had been a righteous man, but zealous pride (hamiyyah) carried him away. He said to Sa'd: "You lie, by the life of Allah, you will not kill him and you are not able to kill him. Had he been of your own clan, you would not have liked him to be killed."' Then Usayd ibn Hudayr, who was a cousin of Sa'd, stood up and said to Sa'd ibn Ubadah: 'You lie, by the life of Allah, we will certainly kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of hypocrites.'" She said: "The two factions, the Aws and the Khazraj, were stirred up until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit. She said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to calm them until they fell silent, and he fell silent.'"

She said: "I wept that whole day; my tears did not cease and I did not sleep. [She said: 'My parents were with me in the morning, and I had wept for two nights and a day, not sleeping, and my tears not ceasing, until I thought that weeping would split my liver. While my parents were sitting with me, and I was weeping, a woman of the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, and I permitted her, and she sat weeping with me.'] [[Omitted from "a".]]"

She said: "While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted, then sat down. She said: 'He had not sat with me since what was said was said, and he had remained a month without any revelation coming to him concerning my matter.' She said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the tashahhud when he sat, then said: "As to what follows, O Aishah, it has reached me that such and such was said about you. If you are innocent, Allah will clear you. And if you have fallen into sin, then ask forgiveness of Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance."'"

She said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished speaking, my tears dried up until I could not feel a single drop. So I said to my father, "Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on what he said." My father said, "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." Then I said to my mother, "Answer the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on what he said." She said, "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." So I said, being a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an: "By Allah, I know that you have heard this report until it has settled in your minds and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent, you will not believe me, and if I confess to you a matter which Allah knows I am innocent of, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except the words of Abu Yusuf: ﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the one whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [Yusuf: 18]." Then I turned over and lay down on my bed, and I knew, and Allah knew, that I was innocent at that time, and that Allah would clear me by my innocence. But by Allah, I did not think that Allah would send down in my case a revelation to be recited. My affair in my own eyes was too insignificant for Allah to speak about me concerning it. Rather, I hoped that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would see in a dream a vision by which Allah would clear me. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not moved from his place, and no one from the household had left, when revelation came down upon him. He was seized by the distress that used to seize him, until the sweat would pour from him like pearls, even though it was a winter day, because of the weight of the word that was being sent down to him. She said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was relieved, and he was smiling. The first word he spoke was, "O Aisha, by Allah, Allah has cleared you." She said: My mother said to me, "Get up and go to him." I said, "By Allah, I will not get up to him, for I praise none but Allah." She said: Then Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a faction among you﴾ [al-Nur: 11], the ten verses. When Allah sent down my innocence, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who used to spend on Mistah ibn Uthathah because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend on Mistah anything again after what he said about Aisha." So Allah sent down: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give﴾ [al-Nur: 22], up to His words ﴿Forgiving, Merciful﴾. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: "Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me." So he restored to Mistah the provision that he used to spend on him, and said: "By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him, ever."

Aisha said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about my affair. He said to Zaynab, "What do you know or what have you seen?" She said, "O Messenger of Allah, I guard my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing but good." Aisha said: She was the one who competed with me among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, but Allah protected her by her piety. She said: Her sister Hamnah began to fight on her behalf, and she was destroyed along with those who were destroyed.

Ibn Shihab (al-Zuhri) said: This is what has reached me of the report of these men. Aisha said: By Allah, the man who was accused said: "Glory be to Allah! By Him in whose hand is my soul, I have never uncovered the veil of any woman." She said: Then he was killed afterwards in the way of Allah. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter "The Hadith of al-Ifk" (7/431-435), and in Tafsir Surat al-Nur (8/452-455), and in al-Shahadat (5/269-272), and in other places. Muslim narrated it in al-Tawbah, chapter "On the Hadith of al-Ifk and the Acceptance of the Repentance of the Slanderer," no. 2770 (4/2129-2136). The author cited its beginning in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/153).]

Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated it from Yahya ibn Bukayr, who related from al-Layth, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, with a similar chain, and he said: "If you have committed some sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance," up to his words "she was destroyed along with those of the slanderers who were destroyed." [Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Tafsir, Surat al-Nur (8/452-455).]

Abu Usama narrated from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to my house and asked about my servant girl. She said: "No, by Allah, I know of no fault in her except that she would sleep until a sheep came in and ate her leavened dough or her kneaded dough." Some of his companions rebuked her, and he said, "Speak the truth to the Messenger of Allah," until they dropped her dignity. She said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I know nothing of her except what a goldsmith knows of pure red gold." In the same report she said: "Revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and then was lifted from him, and I could see the joy on his face as he wiped his forehead and said, 'Rejoice, O Aisha, for Allah has sent down your innocence.'" My parents said to me, "Get up and go to him." I said, "No, by Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise him, nor will I praise anyone, but I praise Allah who has cleared me. You heard it, and you did not deny it or change it." [Al-Bukhari related it as a suspended report in the form of a definite statement, in the chapter "Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread..." (8/488). Muslim also narrated it in al-Tawbah (4/2137-2138).]

As for the explanation of His words ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾: al-ifk is falsehood, and al-ifk is the worst of falsehood. It was named ifk because it is turned away from the truth, from their saying "afaka al-shay'" when one turns a thing away from its face. This is because Aisha deserved praise for her chastity and nobility, so whoever accused her of evil turned the matter away from its proper face. ﴿A faction among you﴾ means a group from among you, including Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Mistah ibn Uthathah, Hassan ibn Thabit, Hamnah bint Jahsh, the wife of Talhah ibn Ubayd Allah, and others. ﴿Do not consider it bad for you﴾, O Aisha and O Safwan. It was said that it is addressed to Aisha, her parents, the Prophet ﷺ, and Safwan, meaning: do not consider the slander to be an evil for you. ﴿Rather, it is good for you﴾, because Allah will reward you for it and make your innocence manifest.

﴿For every person among them﴾, meaning among the lying faction, ﴿is what he has earned of sin﴾, meaning the recompense for the sin he committed in proportion to his involvement in it. ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part thereof﴾, meaning he bore most of it and was the first to plunge into it. Yaqub read "kibrahu" with a damma on the kaf, while the majority read it with a kasra. Al-Kisa'i said: both are dialects. Al-Dahhak said: he is the one who undertook spreading the report, and he is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

Al-Zuhri narrated from Urwa, from Aisha, concerning ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part of it among them﴾: she said, "It was Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul." [See al-Bukhari (8/450, 452) and Sahih Muslim (4/2131).] ﴿And for him is a painful punishment﴾ is the Fire in the Hereafter.

Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from Urwa, from Aisha, in the hadith of al-Ifk, that she said: "Then I rode, and Safwan took the reins, and we passed by a group of hypocrites. It was their custom to stop away from the people. Abdullah ibn Ubayy, their leader, said, 'Who is this?' They said, 'Aisha.' He said, 'By Allah, she has not escaped from him, nor has he escaped from her. She is the wife of your Prophet, who spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her.'" [See Fath al-Bari (8/461).] Hassan, Mistah, and Hamnah also began to spread it, so those who took upon themselves the greater part of it were concerned.

Some people said: it is Hassan ibn Thabit. We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Isma'il, who was informed by Bishr ibn Khalid, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: I entered upon Aisha and Hassan ibn Thabit was with her, reciting poetry in which he mentioned some verses of his own about her, saying:

"She is chaste and steadfast; she is not accused of doubt,
and she wakes up free from the flesh of the heedless."

[Al-hasan: the chaste woman. Al-razan: the sedate one, firm, not moved by frivolity. Tuzann: is accused and suspected. Al-rayb: suspicion and accusation. Gharthaa: hungry, meaning she does not backbite women. Al-ghawafil: plural of ghafilah, the one whose heart is heedless of evil.]

Aisha said to him: "But you are not like that." Masruq said: I said to her, "Why do you permit him to enter upon you, when Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part thereof will have a great punishment﴾?" She said: "And what punishment is greater than blindness?" And she said: "He used to defend or retaliate with poetry on behalf of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [Al-Bukhari narrated it in Tafsir, chapter "And Allah makes clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise" (8/485).]

[Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said (3/273): "Most scholars hold that what is meant by 'he who took upon himself the greater part of it' is Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may Allah curse him, and he is the one whose identity was previously stated in the hadith. This was said by Mujahid and others. It was also said that it refers to Hassan ibn Thabit, but this is a strange view. Had it not appeared in Sahih al-Bukhari in a way that may suggest it, its mention would be of little benefit, for he is among the Companions who have virtues and merits, and his finest achievement is that he defended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his poetry..."]

It is also narrated that the Prophet ﷺ ordered that those who accused Aisha be given the prescribed punishment, eighty lashes each. [See Fath al-Bari (8/479) and Zad al-Ma'ad fi Huda Khayr al-Ibad by Ibn al-Qayyim (3/263-264).]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why did not﴾ (lawla), meaning "why did not" (halla), ﴿when you heard it, the believing men and believing women think well of their own kind﴾ (bi-anfusihim), meaning of their brothers, ﴿good﴾ (khayran). Al-Hasan said: "Of the people of their religion, because the believers are like one soul." Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [an-Nisa: 29], and "greet one another" [an-Nur: 61].

﴿And they said, "This is a clear lie."﴾ That is, a manifest falsehood.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 13–14:

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ That is, according to what they claimed. ﴿Since they did not bring the witnesses, then those, with Allah, they are the liars.﴾ If it is asked: how can they become liars in the sight of Allah when they did not bring the witnesses, and whoever lies is a liar in the sight of Allah whether or not he brings witnesses? It is said: "In the sight of Allah" means in the judgment of Allah. It is also said: its meaning is, "Deny them by the command of Allah." It is also said: this refers to 'Aisha, and its meaning is: "Those are the liars concerning what is unseen to Me and known to Me."

﴿Had it not been for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into﴾, meaning, what you engaged in, ﴿concerning it﴾, of the slander (ifk), ﴿a great punishment.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, a punishment without end, meaning in the Hereafter, because He mentioned the punishment of this world before, saying, ﴿And the one among them who took upon himself the greater part of it, for him is a great punishment﴾. And it did befall him, for he was flogged and subjected to the prescribed punishment (hadd). 'Amrah narrated from 'Aisha that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) applied the prescribed punishment to four persons: 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh.[[Al-Tirmidhi narrated from 'Aisha, who said: "When my innocence was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood on the minbar, mentioned that, and recited the Qur'an. When it was revealed, he commanded that two men and a woman be punished, and they were flogged for their penalty." Tafsir Surat al-Nur: 9/37. He said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we do not know except through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq." The naming of these three—Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh—occurs in Abu Dawud, in the Book of Hudud, chapter on the punishment for slander: 6/283. Al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i and said: "Ibn Ishaq traced it once and sent it as mursal another time." It was also narrated by Ibn Majah in the Book of Hudud, chapter on the punishment for slander: 2/857. See also Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/272. Al-Tabarani narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr a similar hadith to that of 'Aisha which the author cited. Al-Haythami said: "It contains Ibn Lahi'ah, who is weak, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/80. See also Fath al-Bari: 9/481, Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 9/37. Al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a hasan chain, from Abu Hurairah, and in it: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) applied the prescribed punishment to Mistah, Hamnah, and Hassan." See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/146, and consult Zad al-Ma'ad: 3/263–264.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 15–19:

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾, meaning: you were saying it. ﴿And said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge﴾. Mujahid and Muqatil said: some of you would relate it from others. Al-Kalbi said: this was because a man among them would meet another and say, "It has reached me that such and such," and they would receive it from one another (yatalaqqawnahu talaqqiyyan). Al-Zajjaj said: some of you would throw it (yulqihi) to others. A-isha recited "tilaqawnahu" with a kasra on the lam and a light qaf, from al-walaq, which means lying. ﴿And you say with your mouths what is not for you to know, and you think it is trivial﴾, meaning: you suppose it is easy, with no sin in it. ﴿And it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous﴾, meaning in its burden of sin.

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You [above such things]! This is a great slander"?﴾ The word "subhanaka" here means amazement (al-ta'ajjub). ﴿This is a great slander﴾, meaning: a great lie that astonishes and bewilders people because of its enormity. In some reports, Umm Ayyub said to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: "Have you not heard what people are saying about A-isha?" Abu Ayyub said: "Subhanaka, this is a great slander" [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 373; see also al-Tabari 18/96, al-Durr al-Manthur 6/159, Fath al-Bari 9/470.]] So the verse was revealed in accordance with his words.

﴿Allah admonishes you﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Allah forbids you. Mujahid said: Allah prohibits you.

﴿That you never return to the like of it again, if you are believers﴾. ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ concerning command and prohibition. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the matter of A-isha and Safwan, ﴿All-Wise﴾, who judged their innocence.

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who love that immorality spread﴾, meaning: become public, and fornication be broadcast, ﴿among those who believe – for them is a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter﴾, meaning Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his hypocritical companions. The punishment in this world is the prescribed penalty (al-hadd), and in the Hereafter, the Fire. ﴿And Allah knows﴾ their lying and the innocence of A-isha, and what they plunged into of the wrath of Allah, ﴿while you know not﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 20–22:

﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Most Kind, Most Merciful.﴾ The response (jawab) of "lawla" (had it not been) is omitted, meaning: He would have hastened the punishment upon you. Ibn 'Abbas said: he means Mistah, Hassan, and Hamnah.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Whoever follows the footsteps of Satan, indeed he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing.﴾ "Immorality" means the vile deeds, and "wrongdoing" means what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, detests. ﴿And had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified.﴾ Mujahid said: "would not have been made righteous." Ibn Qutaybah said: "would not have been cleansed." ﴿Among you, any one of you.﴾ According to some exegetes, the verse is general. They said: Allah informs that, had it not been for His bounty and His mercy in protecting (ʿiṣmah, divine preservation from sin), none of you would have become righteous. Others said: this address is to those who engaged in the slander (al-ifk), and its meaning is: he would not be purified from this sin, nor would his affair be set right after what he did. This is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of ʿAṭāʾ, who said: "He would never accept the repentance of any one of you." ﴿Ever. But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, meaning He cleanses from sin by mercy and forgiveness. ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear...﴾ meaning: let them not swear. It is a form of "yaftaʿil" from "al-ulyah," which means an oath. Abu Jaʿfar recited "yata'alla" with the "ta'" placed first and the hamzah delayed, which is a form of "yatafaʿʿal" from "al-ulyah."

﴿Those of virtue among you and of wealth﴾ means Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. ﴿Let them not give to the near of kin, the needy, and those who emigrated in the way of Allah﴾ means Mistah, who was a needy emigrant (muhajir) who had fought at Badr (badri), and was a cousin on his mother's side of Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr had sworn that he would not spend on him. ﴿And let them pardon and overlook﴾ their immersion in the matter of ʿAʾishah. ﴿Do you not love﴾ — addressing Abu Bakr — ﴿that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ When the Prophet ﷺ recited it to Abu Bakr, he said: "Yes, I love that Allah should forgive me." He then restored to Mistah the support that he used to give him, and said: "By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him, ever."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter: "Why, when you heard it, did you not say: it is not for us to speak of this; glory be to You, this is a great slander" (8/455), and by Muslim in Repentance, chapter on the hadith of the slander and the acceptance of the repentance of the slanderer, no. (2770): 4/2129–2136.]]

Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: some of the Companions, among them Abu Bakr, swore that they would not give charity to a man who had spoken something of the slander, nor would they benefit them. So Allah revealed this verse.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/102–103.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste women﴾ (al-muhsanat), meaning the chaste, ﴿unaware﴾ (al-ghafilat) of immoral acts, ﴿believing﴾ (al-mu'minat). One who is "unaware" of immorality means that no act of immorality has entered her heart, and ʿĀʾishah was such. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter﴾, meaning they are punished with the prescribed penalties (hudud) in this world, and with the Fire in the Hereafter. ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾. Muqatil said: this refers to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, the hypocrite. It is related from Khasif who said: I said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr: "Whoever slanders a believing woman, will Allah curse him in this world and the Hereafter?" He said: "That applies to ʿĀʾishah specifically."[[Al-Suyuti attributed it (6/164) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani. Al-Haythami said (6/79): al-Tabarani narrated it, and in it is Yahya al-Hammani, who is weak.]]

Others said: it refers specifically to ʿĀʾishah and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, to the exclusion of all other believing women. It is related from al-ʿAwwam ibn Hawshab, from a shaykh of the Banu Kahil, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "This was revealed concerning ʿĀʾishah and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ specifically; there is no repentance for it. Whoever slanders a believing woman, Allah has made repentance available to him," and then he recited: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ up to His saying: ﴿except those who repent﴾. Thus He made repentance for these, and did not make repentance for those.[[Al-Haythami said (6/80): "Al-Tabarani narrated it through several chains; in this chain there is a narrator who is not named, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy, and it is the best of these chains."]]

Others said: this verse was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and that [[In manuscript B: "kadhalika hatta" (thus, until).]] was when the verse at the beginning of the surah was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ up to His saying: ﴿indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. So Allah revealed the lashing and repentance.[[al-Tabari mentioned these opinions (18/104-105), then gave preference, saying: "The most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: this verse was revealed concerning ʿĀʾishah, and its ruling is general to everyone who has the attribute that Allah described in it."]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 24, verses 24–26:**

﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *yashhadu* with the *ya'* (ي), because the verb is placed before its subject. The others read it with the *ta'* (ت), *tashhadu*. ﴿Their tongues﴾: this is before the mouths are sealed. ﴿Their hands and their feet﴾: it is narrated that the mouths will be sealed, so the hands and feet will speak of what they did in the world. It was also said: the meaning is that the tongues of some of them will bear witness against others, and their hands and feet will bear witness too. ﴿Concerning what they used to do.﴾ ﴿On that day Allah will pay them their full recompense in truth﴾: their due reward. It was also said: their just reckoning.

﴿And they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth﴾: He will make clear to them the reality of what He promised them in the world. Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: This is because Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to doubt the religion, so on the Day of Resurrection he will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Evil words are for evil men﴾. Most of the exegetes said: the evil words, meaning the evil speech and talk, are for evil men among people.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 27:

His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you have asked permission and greeted their occupants. That is better for you, so that you may remember.﴾ It has been said: the meaning of His saying ﴿until you have asked permission [tasta'nisu]﴾ is: until you seek permission [tasta'dhinu]. [Ibn 'Abbas used to recite "until you seek permission (hatta tasta'dhinu)" and would say: "tasta'nisu" is a mistake of the scribe.] [[Missing from manuscript "A".]] [[See the earlier commentary: 3/309, 310.]] Likewise Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to recite it. The well-known recitation, however, is "tasta'nisu," and it carries the meaning of seeking permission. It has also been said: al-isti'nas (seeking familiarity/permission) is seeking to know whether there is a person in the house, so that one informs them, "I am entering." Al-Khalil said: al-istinas is al-istibsar (looking to see), from the saying "anastu naran," meaning "I saw a fire." It has also been said: it is that one makes a sound with a tasbih (saying "Subhan Allah"), or a takbir (saying "Allahu akbar"), or clears one's throat, thereby informing the people of the house.

The summary of the ruling of the verse: one does not enter another's house except after greeting and asking permission. They differed over whether one should begin with asking permission or with the greeting. A people said: one begins with asking permission, saying, "May I enter? Peace be upon you," based on His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿until you have asked permission [tasta'nisu]﴾, meaning, ﴿seek permission [tasta'dhinu]﴾, ﴿and greet the occupants﴾. But most scholars hold that one begins with the greeting, saying, "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" In the verse there is an inversion of order, its implied sense being: "until you greet its occupants and seek permission." Likewise it is in the codex of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. It is narrated from Kaladah ibn Hanbal who said: "I entered upon the Prophet ﷺ without greeting and without asking permission, and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Go back and say: Peace be upon you, may I enter?'" [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter: How to ask permission: 8/56-57; al-Tirmidhi in al-Isti'dhan, what has come concerning greeting before asking permission: 7/490-491, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except through the hadith of Ibn Jurayj. Abu 'Asim narrated it from Ibn Jurayj in like manner." Also Imam Ahmad: 3/414, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/284.]]

It is narrated from Ibn 'Umar that a man asked permission to enter upon him, saying, "May I enter?" Ibn 'Umar said, "No." Then some of them instructed the man to greet, so he greeted and was given permission. [[Related by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/383, and mentioned by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/284.]]

Some said: if his gaze falls upon a person, he begins with the greeting; otherwise he begins with asking permission, then greets. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and Hudhayfah said: one asks permission before entering upon those who are within the prohibited degrees (dhawat al-mahram), and similarly it is reported from al-Hasan. And if they are in one house, he should clear his throat and make some slight movement.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad 'Abd Allah ibn Bishran informed us; Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us; Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi informed us; 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Ma'mar informed us, from Sa'id al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Qays greeted 'Umar ibn al-Khattab three times, but he was not given permission, so he returned. 'Umar sent after him and said, "Why did you return?" He said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'If one of you greets three times and is not answered, let him return.'" 'Umar said, "You must bring evidence for what you say, or I will do such-and-such to you," but he had threatened him. He said: Then Abu Musa al-Ash'ari came, his color pale, while I was sitting in a circle, and we said, "What is the matter with you?" He said, "I greeted 'Umar," and he informed us of his account. "Did any of you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" They said, "Yes, all of us heard it." So they sent with him a man from among them until he came to 'Umar and informed him of that. [[See the narration in al-Jami' of Imam Ma'mar: 10/380, and it is in the two Shaykhs (Bukhari and Muslim), as will come in the following note.]]

Busr ibn Sa'id narrated it from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and in it: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If one of you asks permission three times and is not given permission, let him return." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Isti'dhan, chapter: Greeting and asking permission three times: 11/26-27, and in other places; and Muslim in al-Adab, chapter on asking permission, no. (2153): 3/1694; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/280-281.]] Al-Hasan said: The first is an announcement, the second is consultation, and the third is asking permission to leave.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 28:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿But if you find no one therein, then do not enter them⦆ meaning: if you do not find in the houses anyone who gives you permission to enter them, then do not enter them, ﴿until permission is given to you. And if you are told, "Go back," then go back.﴾ meaning: if there are people in the house and they say, "Go back," then let him go back and not stand at the door persistently. ﴿It is purer for you﴾ meaning: going back is more pure and more proper for you. Qatadah said: If he is not given permission, let him not sit at the door, for people have needs. If he arrives and does not ask permission but sits at the door waiting, that is permissible.

Ibn Abbas used to come to the door of the Ansar seeking knowledge (hadith), and he would sit at the door until the man came out, without asking permission. The man would come out and say, "O cousin of the Messenger of Allah, if only you had informed me!" He would say, "This is how we were commanded to seek knowledge." [[Narrated by Ibn Abd al-Barr with his full chain in Jami' Bayan al-Ilm wa Fadlihi, p. (140).]] And when he stands, he should not look through a gap in the door if the door is closed. Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu al-Husayn ibn Bishran informed us: Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, that a man looked at the Prophet ﷺ through a gap in the curtain of the chamber while the Prophet ﷺ had a comb (midra) in his hand. [[The midra is of two kinds: one small, made of ebony, ivory or iron, the length of a needle, used only for parting the hair, with a round head shaped like a sword blade; and another large, a cone-shaped piece of ebony or other wood, with a carved head about the size of a palm, having fingers-like teeth, the first of which is curved like the ring of a thumb used for combing.]] He said: "If I had known that this man was looking at me until I came to him, I would have jabbed the comb into his eyes. Was permission not ordained only for the sake of sight?" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Diyat, chapter: "Whoever looks into the house of a people and they gouge out his eye, there is no blood-money for him," 12/243, and by Muslim in Adab, chapter on the prohibition of looking into another's house, no. (2156), 3/1698.]]

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a man looks at you without permission and you strike him with a pebble and blind his eye, there is no blame upon you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Diyat, chapter: "Whoever looks into the house of a people and they gouge out his eye, there is no blood-money for him," 12/243, and by Muslim in Adab, chapter on the prohibition of looking into another's house, no. (2158), 3/1699; also al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 10/254, and al-Shafi'i 2/101.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what you do﴾, of entering with permission and without permission. When the verse of seeking permission was revealed, they said: "What about the houses between Makkah and Madinah and Syria, and along the road, which have no residents?" So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed:

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 29–30:

﴿There is no blame upon you that you enter houses not inhabited, wherein is provision for you﴾ [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (the occasions of revelation), p. 375. See also al-Qurtubi: 12/213.]]. That is, without seeking permission. ﴿Wherein is provision for you﴾ means benefit for you. The scholars differed concerning these houses. Qatadah said: They are the caravanserais (khanat), the houses and the dwellings built for travellers (al-sabilah), so that they may take shelter in them and store their goods in them. Entering them is permitted without seeking permission, and the benefit in them is in lodging, sheltering goods, and protection from heat and cold.

Ibn Zayd said: They are the shops of merchants and their stalls in the markets, which they enter for buying and selling, and this is the benefit. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: There is no need for permission (idhn) for the shops of the market. Ibn Sirin, whenever he came to a shop in the market, would say: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" Then he would go in. Ata' said: They are the ruined houses, and the provision is relieving oneself in them of urine and excrement. It has also been said: They are the houses that have no occupant, because seeking permission was only prescribed so that one would not look upon something private (awrah). If that is not feared, then one may enter without seeking permission [[These sayings were mentioned by al-Tabari: 18/113–116.]]. ﴿And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal﴾.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Say to the believing men that they should lower some of their gaze﴾, that is, from looking at what it is not lawful to look upon. It has been said that "min" (some) is a sila (a redundant particle), meaning: that they lower their gaze. It has also been said that it is affirmative, because believers are not commanded to lower the gaze in absolute terms, since lowering the gaze is not obligatory regarding what is lawful to look upon; rather, they are commanded to lower it from what is not lawful to look upon. ﴿And that they guard their private parts﴾ from what is not lawful. Abu al-Aliyah said: Every mention of guarding the private parts in the Qur'an refers to fornication and what is unlawful, except in this place, where he intended by it concealment, so that the sight of another does not fall upon it. ﴿That﴾, that is, lowering the gaze and guarding the private parts, ﴿is purer for them﴾, that is, better for them and more pure. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Aware of what they do﴾, Knowing of what they do.

It is narrated from Buraydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Ali: "O Ali, do not let a glance follow a glance, for the first is yours, but the second is not yours" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Nikah, chapter: What one is commanded regarding lowering the gaze: 3/70. Al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter: What has come concerning the sudden glance: 8/61, and he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we know only through the narration of Shurayk. Al-Darimi in al-Riqaq, chapter: On guarding the hearing: 2/298. Al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/194, according to the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Imam Ahmad: 5/353, 357. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/23.]].

It is narrated from Jarir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the sudden glance, and he said: "Turn your gaze away" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Adab, chapter: The sudden glance, no. (2159): 3/1699. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/23.]].

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us, from al-Dahhak ibn Uthman, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man should not look at the private part (awrah) of a man, and a woman should not look at the private part of a woman. It is narrated from Jarir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the sudden glance, and he said: "Turn your gaze away" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Adab, chapter: The sudden glance, no. (2159): 3/1699. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/23.]].

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us, from al-Dahhak ibn Uthman, who said: Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man should not look at the private part (awrah) of a man, and a woman should not look at the private part of a woman. A man should not lie with a man under one garment, and a woman should not lie with a woman under one garment" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Hayd, chapter: The prohibition of looking at private parts, no. (338): 1/266. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/20.]].

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 31 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze﴾ from what is not lawful, ﴿and guard their private parts﴾ from those who are not lawful to them. It has also been said: "and guard their private parts" means: they should cover them so that no one sees them. It is narrated from Umm Salamah that she was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Maymunah when Ibn Umm Maktum came and entered upon him. This was after we had been commanded to observe hijab. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Veil yourselves from him." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is he not blind, so that he cannot see us?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are you two blind? Do you not see him?" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Libas, chapter on His saying, "And tell the believing women to lower their gaze" (6/60-61); al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter on what has been related about women veiling from men (8/61-62), and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i. Ahmad narrated it (6/296), and the author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/24).
Abu Dawud said: "This applies specifically to the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ). Do you not see that Fatimah bint Qays observed her waiting period (iddah) at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, and the Prophet (ﷺ) had said to Fatimah bint Qays: 'Observe your waiting period at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man, you may put off your clothes in his presence'?" See 'Awn al-Ma'bud (11/170).]] His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and not to reveal their adornment﴾, that is, not to display their adornment to non-mahrams (those whom it is forbidden to marry because of close kinship). By this he means the hidden adornment. Adornment is of two kinds: hidden and apparent. The hidden is like the anklet, henna on the feet, the bracelet on the wrist, the earring, and necklaces. It is not permissible for her to display these, nor for a non-mahram to look at them. By "adornment" is meant the place of adornment.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿except what appears thereof﴾, he means by this the apparent adornment. The scholars differed concerning this apparent adornment which Allah has excepted. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and al-Awza'i said: it is the face and the two palms.
