Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the clothing, based on the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Take your adornment at every place of worship﴾ [al-A'raf: 31], and by it he meant clothing. Al-Hasan said: the face and the clothing. Ibn 'Abbas said: kohl, the ring, and henna on the palm.

Whatever is of the apparent adornment, it is permissible for a non-mahram man to look at it, provided he does not fear temptation and desire. If he fears any of these, he should lower his gaze. This allowance for what a woman may reveal of her body is granted because it is not 'awrah (the parts of the body that must be covered), and she is commanded to uncover it in prayer, whereas the rest of her body is 'awrah, which she must cover.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾, that is: let them throw their veils [over their chests], ﴿over their bosoms﴾ and their chests [so that by this they cover their hair, their chests] [[The words between the brackets are omitted from manuscript "A".]], their necks and their earrings. 'A'ishah said: "May Allah have mercy on the first women of the Muhajirat. When Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And let them draw their head-coverings over their bosoms﴾, they tore their cloaks and covered themselves with them." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter on "And let them draw their head-coverings over their bosoms" (8/489).]]

﴿And not to reveal their adornment﴾, meaning the hidden adornment, which it is not permitted for them to uncover in prayer or before non-mahram men, and that is everything other than the face and the two palms. ﴿except to their husbands﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: this means they should not remove the jilbab or the khimar except before their husbands, that is, their spouses; ﴿or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers﴾. It is permissible for these to look at the hidden adornment, but they should not look at what lies between the navel and the knee. It is permissible for a husband to look at her entire body, except that it is disliked for him to look at her private part.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or their women﴾. He means that it is permissible for a woman to look at the body of another woman, except what lies between the navel and the knee, just as a mahram man may. This applies when the woman is Muslim. If she is a non-Muslim, is it permissible for a Muslim woman to uncover herself before her? The scholars differed on this. Some said: it is permissible, just as it is permissible for her to uncover herself before a Muslim woman, since she is among the women. Others said: it is not permissible, because Allah, exalted is He, said: "or their women," and a non-Muslim woman is not among our women, and because she is a stranger in religion, so she is further removed than a non-mahram man. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah instructing him to prevent the women of the People of the Book from entering the bathhouse with Muslim women. [[Narrated by al-Tabari (18/121). al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/183) attributed it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or those whom their right hands possess﴾. The scholars differed concerning this. A group said: a woman's male slave is a mahram to her, so it is permissible for him to enter upon her if he is chaste, and to look at the body of his mistress except what lies between the navel and the knee, like the mahrams, and this is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. This was narrated from 'A'ishah and Umm Salamah. Thabit narrated from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Fatimah with a slave whom he had given her. Fatimah was wearing a garment which, when she covered her head with it, did not reach her feet, and when she covered her feet, did not reach her head. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw what she was facing, he said: "There is no harm for you; he is only your father and your servant." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Libas, chapter on the slave looking at the hair of his mistress (6/59). Al-Mundhiri said: "Its isnad includes Abu Jami' Salim ibn Dinar al-Hujaymi al-Basri. Ibn Ma'in said: he is reliable. Abu Zur'ah al-Razi said: he is Egyptian, weak in narration, and he is Salim ibn Abi Rashid." Al-Bayhaqi narrated it (7/95), and al-Albani graded it sahih in al-Irwa' (6/206).]] Others said: he is like a non-mahram man in her presence. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: the verse refers only to female slaves (imaa') and not to male slaves. Ibn Jurayj said regarding "or their women, or those whom their right hands possess" that it is not lawful for a Muslim woman to undress before a polytheist woman, unless that polytheist woman is her slave girl.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or male attendants who have no physical desire﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read "ghayra" with a fatha on the ra', as an exception (qat'), because "al-tabi'in" is definite and "ghayr" is indefinite. It has also been said that it has the meaning of "illa" (except), so it is an exception, meaning: they may reveal their adornment to the male attendants, except those among them who have physical desire, for they may not reveal their adornment to those among them who have desire. The others read it with a kasra, as an attributive adjective (na't) of "al-tabi'in." The word "al-irbah" and "al-arab" means need. The meaning of "the male attendants who have no physical desire" is those who follow the people in order to obtain some of their leftover food, having no aspiration except that, and no need for women. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and al-Sha'bi. It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it refers to the foolish impotent man. Al-Hasan said: it is the one who cannot achieve an erection, is unable to have intercourse with women, and has no desire for them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is the mentally deficient. 'Ikrimah said: it is the one whose genitals have been cut off. It has been said: it is the effeminate man. Muqatil said: the decrepit old man, the impotent, the eunuch, the one whose genitals have been cut off, and the like.

Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us; Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri informed us; Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ma'qil ibn Muhammad al-Maydani informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us; 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah who said: A man, an effeminate man (mukhannath), used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they used to count him among the male attendants who have no physical desire. One day the Prophet (ﷺ) entered while he was with some of his wives, and he was describing a woman, saying: "When she comes forward, she comes with four [folds of flesh], and when she turns away, she turns away with eight." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do I not see that this man knows what is here? Do not let this man enter upon you." So they veiled him from them. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Libas, chapter on expelling those who imitate women from houses, from Umm Salamah (10/333); Muslim in al-Salam, chapter on prohibiting the effeminate man from entering upon non-mahram women, no. (2181) (4/1716); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (12/122).]]

﴿or children who have not yet attained knowledge of women's private parts﴾. By "children" he means the young ones, which may be singular or plural, meaning: they have not uncovered the private parts of women through sexual intercourse so as to look upon them. It has also been said: they do not yet know the 'awrah from other things because of their young age. This is the view of Mujahid. It has also been said: they are not yet capable of matters concerning women. It has also been said: they have not yet reached the age of sexual desire.

﴿And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they conceal of their adornment﴾. A woman used to strike her foot when walking so that the sound of her anklet would be heard or her anklet would be noticed, so she was forbidden from doing so.

﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you﴾ from the shortcoming that occurs in obeying His command and prohibition. It has also been said: return to obedience to Allah in what He has commanded you and forbidden you concerning the etiquette mentioned in this surah. ﴿O believers, perhaps you will be successful﴾. Ibn 'Amir read: "ayyuh al-mu'minun" and "ya ayyuh al-sahir" and "ayyuh al-thaqalan," with a damma on the ha' in all of them, and he stops without an alif according to the written form. The others read with a fatha on the ha's, according to the original form. 

Abu al-Hasan informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi; Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Huzaym al-Shashi informed us; Abu Muhammad 'Abd ibn Humayd al-Kashshi informed us; Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to me; 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, turn to your Lord in repentance, for I turn to my Lord a hundred times each day." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Dhikr wal-Du'a' wal-Istighfar, chapter on the recommendation of seeking forgiveness and increasing it, no. (2072) (4/2076); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (5/71).]]

Abu al-Hasan informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi; Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hamawayh al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Huzaym al-Shashi informed us; Abu Muhammad 'Abd ibn Humayd al-Kashshi informed us; Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to me; 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us, from Malik ibn Mighwal, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: We used to count for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the gathering, as he said: "My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance, for You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful," one hundred times. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salah, chapter on seeking forgiveness (2/151); al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter on what one says when rising from his gathering (9/393), and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith." Ibn Majah in al-Adab, chapter on seeking forgiveness, no. (3814); Ahmad in al-Musnad (2/21), and Ibn Hibban graded it sahih, no. (2459), p. (609) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; Abd ibn Humayd narrated it in al-Muntakhab p. (251), and Ibn al-Sunni in 'Amal al-Yawm wal-Layla p. (179). See also Majma' al-Zawa'id (2/113) and Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah (2/89).]]

The summary concerning the 'awrah (parts that must be covered) is this: it is not permissible for the one looking to look at a man's 'awrah, and a man's 'awrah is what lies between the navel and the knee. The same applies to a woman in the presence of a woman. There is no harm in looking at the rest of the body when there is no fear of temptation. Malik and Ibn Abi Dhi'b said: the thigh is not 'awrah, based on what was narrated from 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, who said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) raced a horse in the alleys of Khaybar, and my knee was touching the thigh of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ). Then he pulled up his waist-wrap from his thigh, until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ). [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Salah, chapter on what is mentioned about the thigh (1/479-480) and in other places; Muslim in al-Jihad, chapter on the expedition of Khaybar, no. (1365) (4/1426-1427). The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah (9/21).]]

Most scholars hold that the thigh is an 'awrah (the part of the body that must be covered), based on what Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi reported to us: Abu al-Hasan al-Tays­funi reported to us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari reported to us, Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Hujr reported to us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far reported to us, from al-'Ala' ibn Abi Kathir, from Muhammad ibn Jahsh, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by Ma'mar while his thighs were exposed, and he said: "O Ma'mar, cover your thighs, for the thighs are 'awrah." [[Narrated by al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar: 2/285; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 4/180; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/290. Al-Bukhari cited it in suspended form (mu'allaq): 1/479, and the author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/21.
Al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) said in al-Fath: "Ahmad, the author in al-Tarikh, and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak connected it, all through the route of Isma'il ibn Ja'far from al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from Abu Kathir, the freedman of Muhammad ibn Jahsh, from him..." Shaykh al-Arna'ut authenticated it with its supporting reports in his commentary on Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/21-22.]] It was also reported from Ibn 'Abbas and from Jarhad ibn Khuwaylid, who was one of the People of the Suffah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the thigh is 'awrah." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Permission to Enter (al-Isti'dhan), chapter on what has come that the thigh is 'awrah: 8/78-79, and he said: "This is a hasan hadith; I do not consider its isnad to be connected."
Al-Bukhari narrated it in suspended form: 1/478. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: "The hadith of Jarhad is connected (mawsul) in Malik's Muwatta', and al-Tirmidhi graded it hasan, and Ibn Hibban graded it sahih. The author (al-Baghawi) weakened it in al-Tarikh due to irregularity (idtirab) in its isnad, and I have mentioned many of its routes in Taghliq al-Ta'liq." See also: Mushkil al-Athar: 2/285-286; Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar: 1/474.]]

Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) said: "The hadith of Anas is more firmly supported by its chain (asnad), and the hadith of Jarhad is more cautious (ahwat)." [[In the previous source: 1/478.]] As for a woman with a non-related man: if she is a free woman, then her entire body is 'awrah in relation to a non-related man, and it is not permissible to look at any part of her except the face and the two palms. If she is a slave-woman (amah), then her 'awrah is like the 'awrah of a man, from the navel to the knee. The same applies to close relatives (mahram) with one another. A woman's looking at a non-related man is like his looking at her. A man may look at the entire body of his wife and of his slave-woman whom he is permitted to have, and she likewise may look at him, except for the private part itself, for looking at it is disliked. If a man marries off his slave-woman, it becomes forbidden for him to look at her 'awrah, just like a non-related slave-woman. It was reported from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you marries his slave to his slave-woman, then let him not look at what lies below the navel and above the knee." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Libas, chapter on the saying of Allah, "And say to the believing women that they should lower their gaze...": 6/61; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/226 and 229, and 7/94; and al-Daraqutni: 1/230. Al-Albani graded it hasan in al-Irwa': 2/207. The author mentioned it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/25.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 32:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Marry off the unmarried among you﴾. "Al-ayama" (الْأَيَامَى) is the plural of "ayyim" (أَيِّمٍ), which refers to one who has no spouse, whether a man or a woman. It is said: "rajul ayyim" (a man without a wife) and "imra'ah ayyimah" (a woman without a husband), and "ayyim." The meaning of the verse is: marry off, O believers, those among your free men and women who have no spouse, ﴿and the righteous among your male servants and your female servants﴾. This command is a command of recommendation (nadb) and desirability (istihbab).

It is recommended for one whose soul yearns for marriage and who has the means (uhbat) for marriage to marry. If he does not have the means for marriage, he should subdue his desire through fasting, based on what Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Tusi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Isfara'ini informed us, [saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Mas'ud informed us, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Bajali informed us, Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, Sufyan informed us] from al-A'mash, from Umarah ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of youths, whoever among you is able to marry (al-ba'ah) should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. And whoever is not able, then he should fast, for it is a shield (wija') for him."

And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Marry, so that you multiply, for I shall boast of you before the nations, even of the miscarried fetus."

And he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves my nature (fitrah), let him follow my practice, and marriage is part of my practice."

As for one whose soul does not yearn for marriage while he is able to marry, then devoting himself to worship is better for him than marriage, according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. According to the proponents of personal opinion (ashab al-ra'y), marriage is better.

Al-Shafi'i said: Allah, the Exalted, has mentioned a servant whom He honored, saying: ﴿and a master and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous﴾ (Al 'Imran: 39). "Hasur" (الْحَصُورُ) is one who does not approach women although he is able to. He mentioned the celibate women (al-qawa'id min al-nisa') and did not recommend them to marry.

In the verse there is evidence that the marrying off of unmarried women is to their guardians (awliya'), because Allah, the Exalted, addressed them with it, just as the marrying off of male and female slaves is to their masters, due to His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿and the righteous among your male servants and your female servants﴾. This is the view of the majority of scholars among the Companions and those after them. It is narrated on this authority from Umar, Ali, Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Abd Allah ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah and Aisha. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan, Shurayh, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Umar ibn Abd al-‘Aziz also said this, and al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq adopted it. The proponents of personal opinion permitted a free woman to marry herself off.

Malik said: If the woman is of low standing, it is permissible for her to marry herself off; if she is of noble standing, it is not.

The evidence from the reports that the guardian is a condition is what Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhaladi informed us, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id informed us, Abu Awanah informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no marriage except with a guardian."

[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Marriage, chapter on the guardian: 3/29; al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Marriage, chapter on what has come regarding "no marriage except with a guardian": 4/226-227; Ibn Majah in the Book of Marriage, no. (1881): 1/605; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/169; Ibn Hibban, no. (1243), p. (304); and Imam Ahmad in the Musnad: 4/394.

Al-Tirmidhi said (4/229-234): "The hadith of Abu Musa is a hadith in which there is disagreement..." Then he mentioned the disagreement in its chain, then said: The narration of those who narrated from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There is no marriage except with a guardian," is more authentic in my view, because their hearing from Abu Ishaq was at different times, although Shu'bah and al-Thawri were more retentive and reliable than all those who narrated this hadith from Abu Ishaq... Then he said: "And the practice in this matter is according to the hadith of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'There is no marriage except with a guardian,' among the people of knowledge from the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), including Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abd Allah ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah and others."

Similarly it is narrated from some jurists among the Successors (tabi'un) that they said: "There is no marriage except with a guardian," among them Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan al-Basri, Shurayh, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Umar ibn Abd al-‘Aziz and others. This is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. See: Nasb al-Rayah by al-Zayla'i: 3/182-184.]] Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, Sa'id ibn Salim informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Any woman who marries herself without the permission of her guardian, her marriage is void," three times. "If he has consummated it with her, she is owed the dowry for what he has made lawful of her private part. If they dispute, then the ruler is the guardian of the one who has no guardian."

[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Marriage, chapter on the guardian: 3/26-27; al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Marriage: 4/227-229, and he said: "This is a good hadith, and Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Sufyan al-Thawri, and more than one of the memorizers have narrated something like this from Ibn Jurayj." Also narrated by Ibn Majah in the Book of Marriage, no. (1879): 1/605; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/168 according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim); Ibn Hibban, no. (1248), p. (305) from Mawarid al-Zam'an; al-Bayhaqi: 7/105, 107; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/39.]]

His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing, all-Knowing﴾. It has been said: "richness" (al-ghina) here means contentment (al-qana'ah). It has also been said: it means the combining of two sustenances, the sustenance of the husband and the sustenance of the wife. Umar said: "I am amazed at one who seeks wealth without marriage, when Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾."

[It is narrated from some of them that Allah, the Exalted, promised the wealthy through marriage and through separation, saying: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.]

[[Words in brackets are omitted from manuscript "b".]] And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾ (al-Nisa': 130).

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 24, verse 33:**

﴿And let those who do not find a marriage (nikah) keep themselves chaste﴾, i.e., let those who cannot find the means to marry, for the dowry and maintenance, seek chastity away from the unlawful and from fornication, ﴿until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾, i.e., until Allah grants them abundance of His provision.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who seek a writing (al-kitab) from among those whom your right hands possess, then write (fa-katibuhum) for them﴾, i.e., those who seek the mukatabah (contract of manumission). The occasion of revelation of this verse is what has been narrated: that a slave of Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza asked his master to make a contract of manumission with him, but he refused. So Allah revealed this verse, and Huwaytib made a contract with him for one hundred dinars, and remitted twenty dinars of it for him. He paid it, and was killed on the day of Hunayn in battle.[[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. (375); al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/189; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/184.]]

The kitabah is that a man says to his slave: "I have made a contract of manumission with you for such-and-such an amount of wealth," naming a specific known sum, to be paid in two installments (najmayn) or in known installments, with such-and-such in each installment. "When you have paid, you are free." The slave accepts this. When he pays the wealth, he is freed. The slave becomes entitled to his earnings after the contract (40/a). If he is freed after paying the wealth, whatever surplus remains in his hand of the wealth is his. His children who were born during the period of the contract follow him into freedom. If he is unable to pay the wealth, his master has the right to annul his contract and return him to slavery (riqq), and whatever wealth he has in his hand belongs to his master. This is based on what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', who said: Abdullah ibn Umar used to say: "The mukatab is a slave as long as there remains due from him anything of his contract [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta, as a statement of Ibn Umar, Book of the Mukatab, chapter on judgment concerning the mukatab: 2/787; and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/373.]]." And Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated it from his father, from his grandfather, traced to the Prophet: "The mukatab is a slave as long as there remains due from him a single dirham."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Itq, chapter on the mukatab who pays part of his contract: 5/383. Al-Mundhiri said: in its chain is Isma'il ibn Ayyash, who is weak. Also narrated by al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/372-373.]]

Some of the scholars held that His saying, ﴿then write for them﴾, is a command of obligation: it is obligatory upon the master to make a contract with his slave in whom he knows good, if the slave asks for that, at his value or more. If the slave asks for less than his value, it is not obligatory. This is the view of Ata' and Amr ibn Dinar. It is also based on what is narrated: that Sirin asked Anas ibn Malik to make a contract with him, and he hesitated, so he complained to Umar, who struck him with a whip (al-durrah) and ordered him to make the contract, and he made it.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/126; and Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 8/372; and with similar meaning from Qatadah in al-Bayhaqi: 10/319; al-Bukhari mentions it as a suspended report: 5/184. See also Fath al-Bari: 5/186-187.]] But most scholars held that it is a command of recommendation (nadb) and desirability (istihbab). According to al-Shafi'i, the contract is not permissible for fewer than two installments, because it is a contract permitted for the sake of easing matters for the slave, and part of completing that ease is that the wealth be due to him over a term, so that he may pay it at leisure and the purpose is achieved. This is like the blood money for accidental killing, which is owed by the 'aqilah (paternal kin) as a form of mutual support, and so it was due upon them in deferred installments. Abu Hanifah permitted the contract to be made for a single installment, and immediately (hallah).[[In "a": fa-'allalahu (i.e., he gave a reason for it).]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿if you know in them any good﴾. The scholars differed over the meaning of "good" (khayr). Ibn Umar said: strength for earning. This is the view of Malik and al-Thawri. Al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: wealth, like His saying: ﴿if he leaves behind any wealth (khayran)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 180], i.e., wealth. It is narrated that a slave of Salman al-Farisi said to him: "Make a contract with me." He said: "Do you have wealth?" He said: "No." He said: "Do you want to feed me from the filth of people?" And he did not make the contract with him.[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 8/374; and al-Bayhaqi: 10/320.]] Al-Zajjaj said: "If He had meant wealth, He would have said: 'if you know for them any good.'" Ibrahim, Ibn Zayd and Ubaydah said: truthfulness and trustworthiness.[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq: 8/370, 371; and al-Bayhaqi: 10/318.]] Tawus and Amr ibn Dinar said: wealth and trustworthiness.[[See: Musannaf Abd al-Razzaq: 8/370; and al-Bayhaqi: 10/318.]] Al-Shafi'i said: "The most apparent meanings of good in a slave are: earning together with trustworthiness, so I prefer that he not be prevented from making a contract if he is of this kind."

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us: Abu al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Sharik al-Shafi'i informed us: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us: Abu Bakr al-Jurbadhi informed us: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: al-Layth informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help them: the mukatab who intends to pay, the one who marries seeking chastity, and the one who strives in the way of Allah."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter on what has come concerning the mujahid, the mukatab, and the one who marries: 5/296, and he said: "This is a hasan hadith." Also al-Nasa'i in al-Nikah, chapter on Allah's help for the one who marries and wants chastity: 6/61; Ibn Majah in al-Itq, chapter on the mukatab: 2/841-842; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/160; and al-Baghawi narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/7.]] Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated from Ubaydah: "if you know in them any good," meaning: they establish the prayer.[[Narrated from him by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 8/371.]] It was said: it means that the slave is an adult and sane. As for a child and an insane person, their contract is not valid, because seeking (ibtigha') is not valid from them. Abu Hanifah permitted the contract of a child who is nearing puberty (murahiq).

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. They differed about it. Some of them said: this is an address to the masters: it is obligatory upon the master to remit for his mukatab something of the wealth of the contract. This is the view of Uthman, Ali, al-Zubayr and a group, and al-Shafi'i also held it.

Then they differed about its amount. Some people said: he should remit a quarter of the wealth of the contract. This is the view of Ali, and some narrated it from Ali as a marfu' report.[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq from Ali as marfu': 7/375; and al-Bayhaqi: 10/329. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it by another route as a mawquf report and said: "This is the correct one, a mawquf." Likewise Abd al-Razzaq: 7/376, and al-Tabari: 18/131.]] From Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, he should remit a third. Others said: there is no fixed limit; rather, he should remit whatever he wishes.[[See: al-Tabari: 18/131; al-Musannaf of Abd al-Razzaq: 8/377.]] This is the view of al-Shafi'i.

Nafi' said: Abdullah ibn Umar made a contract with a slave of his for thirty-five thousand dirhams, and he remitted for him five thousand dirhams from the end of the contract.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/131.]] Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: when Ibn Umar made a contract with his mukatab, he did not remit anything of the first installments, out of fear that he might fail to pay, and then his charity would return to him; but he remitted from the last part of the contract whatever he wished.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/131; Abd al-Razzaq: 8/377; and al-Bayhaqi: 3/330.]] Some said: it is a command of recommendation (istihbab). But obligation is more apparent. Some people said: by His saying, "and give them from the wealth of Allah," He meant their share (sahm) which Allah has set for them from the obligatory charities, by His saying: ﴿and for the captives (fi al-riqab)﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60]. This is the view of al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Aslam.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/131-132, and al-Tabari preferred this view, which is the view of those who said it means giving them their share of the obligatory charity. See in detail: 18/132.]] Ibrahim said: it is an exhortation to all people to help them.[[Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq from Ibrahim: 8/376-377.]]

If the mukatab dies before paying the installments, the scholars differed concerning it. Many of them held that he dies as a slave, and the contract is annulled, whether or not he left wealth, just as if the sold item perishes before receipt, the sale is annulled. This is the view of Umar, Ibn Umar, and Zayd ibn Thabit, and Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Zuhri and Qatadah held it, and al-Shafi'i and Ahmad went to it. Others said: if he leaves behind enough to cover what remains of the contract, he is free, and if there is a surplus, the surplus goes to his children who are free. This is the view of Ata', Tawus, al-Nakha'i and al-Hasan, and Malik, al-Thawri and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) also held it. If a master makes a contract with his slave that is invalid (fasidah), the slave is freed upon paying the wealth, because his manumission is contingent upon payment, and it has occurred; and his children and earnings follow him, as in a valid contract. They differ in some rulings: a valid contract, the master does not have the right to annul it unless the mukatab fails to pay the installments, and it is not void upon the master's death, and he is freed by release (ibra') from the installments. An invalid contract, the master has the right to annul it before the payment of the wealth, so that if he pays the wealth after the annulment, he is not freed; it becomes void upon the master's death, and he is not freed by release from the installments. When the mukatab is freed by paying the wealth, recourse (tarajju') does not apply in a valid contract, but it applies in an invalid contract, so the master may claim from him the value of his person, and he may claim from the master what he paid him, if it was wealth.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾. The verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the hypocrite. He had two slave girls, Mu'adhah and Musaykah, and he used to compel them to fornication in exchange for a fee he took from them. This is also what they used to do in the Jahiliyyah: they would hire out their slave women. When Islam came, Mu'adhah said to Musaykah: "This matter we are in does not escape two aspects: if it is good, we have taken enough of it; and if it is evil, it is time for us to abandon it." So Allah revealed this verse.[[Attributed by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (377), to the exegetes; he cited reports that the verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who used to say to a slave girl of his: "Go and bring us something..." and it is in Sahih Muslim.]] It is also narrated that one day one of the two slave girls came with a cloak and the other came with a dinar. He said to them: "Go back and fornicate." They said: "By Allah, we will not do it. Islam has come and has forbidden fornication." So they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complained to him, and so this verse was revealed.[[Narrated by Muqatil: see Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 377-378.]]

﴿And do not compel your slave girls﴾, i.e., your female slaves (imaa'akum), ﴿to prostitution﴾, i.e., fornication, ﴿if they desire chastity﴾, i.e., if they desire it. The meaning is not a condition, because it is not permissible to compel them to fornication even if they do not desire chastity, like His saying: ﴿And you will be superior if you are believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 139], [i.e., if you are believers].[[The phrase in brackets is absent from "b".]] It was said: He stipulated the desire for chastity because compulsion occurs only when they desire chastity; if they do not desire chastity, they commit fornication willingly. Tahassun means taʿaffuf (abstaining/chastity). Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: there is a transposition in the verse, its sense being: "And marry off the single ones among you if they desire chastity, and do not compel your slave girls to prostitution."

﴿That you may seek the goods of the worldly life﴾, i.e., that you may seek some of the wealth of this world, meaning from their earnings and by selling their children. ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning toward the women who were compelled, and the sin is upon the one who compels. Al-Hasan, whenever he recited this verse, would say: "For them, by Allah, for them, by Allah!"

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 34–35 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that make things clear﴾, of the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾, that is, a likeness of your situation to theirs, O deniers. This is a warning to them that there may befall them what befell those deniers before them, ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, the believers who guard against shirk (association of partners with God) and the major sins.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He is the Guide of the people of the heavens and the earth; by His light they are guided to the truth, and by His guidance they are saved from misguidance. Al-Dahhak said: He is the Illuminator of the heavens and the earth. It is said: He illuminated the sky with the angels and illuminated the earth with the prophets. Mujahid said: He is the Manager of affairs in the heavens and the earth. [[Al-Tabari mentioned these three sayings, and he preferred the first, which was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]] Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah said: He is the Adorner of the heavens and the earth. He adorned the sky with the sun, the moon and the stars, and He adorned the earth with the prophets, the scholars and the believers. It is also said: with plants and trees. It was also said: its meaning is that all lights are from Him, just as it is said: "So-and-so is mercy," meaning that mercy comes from him. Such a term may also be used in praise, as the poet said:

*"When 'Abd Allah travels a night from Marw,*
*Its light and its beauty have traveled from it."*

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿the likeness of His light﴾, that is, the likeness of the light of Allah Exalted in the heart of the believer, which is the light by which he is guided, as He said: "So he is upon a light from his Lord" [al-Zumar: 22]. Ibn Mas'ud used to recite: "the likeness of His light in the heart of the believer." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn 'Abbas: the likeness of His light which He gave to the believer. Some said: the pronoun refers to the believer, meaning the likeness of the light of the believer's heart. Ubayy used to recite: "the likeness of the light of one who believed in Him," and he is a servant in whose breast faith and the Qur'an have been placed. Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: by the light is meant the Qur'an. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: by the light is meant obedience; He named obedience to Allah "light" and attributed these lights to Himself as an honour. ﴿Like a niche﴾, and it is the recess that has no opening; if it has an opening, it is a window (kuwwa). It was said: the mishkah is an Abyssinian word. Mujahid said: it is the lamp-stand. [[Al-Tabari said (18/140): "The most correct of the sayings concerning this is the saying of the one who said: it is a parable that Allah struck for the Qur'an in the heart of the people of faith in it. He said: the likeness of the light of Allah, by which He illuminated for His servants the path of right guidance which He sent down to them, so they believed in it and affirmed what is in it, in the hearts of the believers, is like a niche, which is the pillar of the lamp in which is the wick, and that is the counterpart of the recess in the walls that has no opening. That is a likeness of the Qur'an. He says: the Qur'an that is in the heart of the believer, whose heart Allah has illuminated, in his breast; then He likened the breast in its purity from disbelief in Allah and doubt concerning Him, and its being illuminated by the light of the Qur'an, and its being lit by the clear verses of its Lord and its admonitions in it, to a bright star, saying: the glass. That is the breast of the believer, in which is his heart, as if it were a bright star."]] ﴿in it is a lamp﴾, that is, a lantern. Its root is from light, and from it comes "ṣubḥ" (dawn). Its meaning: like a lamp in a niche. ﴿The lamp is in a glass﴾, meaning the lamp-stand. Al-Zajjaj said: he mentioned the glass only because the light and the brightness of the fire within it are clearer than anything else, and its light increases through the glass. Then He described the glass, saying: ﴿the glass is as if it were a glittering star﴾. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read "durri'in" with a kasra on the dal and the hamza. Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with a damma on the dal and the hamza. As for the one who reads it with a kasra on the dal, it is fa'il (the pattern) from al-dar', which means "pushing away," because the star pushes away the devils from the sky. He likened it to the state of being pushed, because in that state it is brighter and more luminous. It is also said: it is from dara'a al-kawkab, when the star moves away, contracting, so its light doubles at that time. It was also said: "durri" means rising, as it is said: daraa al-najm when the star rose and ascended. It is also said: daraa 'alayna fulan, meaning he appeared and became visible. As for raising the dal together with the hamza as Hamzah read, most grammarians said: it is a lahn (a grammatical error; a solecism), because there is no fu'ayl pattern with a damma on the fa' and a kasra on the 'ayn in the speech of the Arabs.

Abu 'Ubayda said: I see a valid form for it, namely that it is durru'un, on the pattern fu'ul from daraat, like subbuh and quddus, and they found the accumulation of dammas heavy, so they changed some of them to a kasra, as they said: 'itiyyan, which is fu'ul from 'atawtu. The others read ﴿durriyyun﴾ with a damma on the dal and a shadda on the ya without a hamza, meaning: very bright, attributed to the pearl (durr) for its purity and beauty. Although the star has more light than a pearl, it surpasses the stars in its brightness, just as a pearl surpasses all other grains. It was also said: the "durri" star is one of the five great planets, which are Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus and Mercury. It was said: He likened it to a star and did not liken it to the sun and the moon, because the sun and the moon are subject to eclipse, while the stars are not subject to eclipse.

﴿Yūqadu﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read "tawaqqada" with a ta' and its vowelling, with a fatha on the waw and the dal, and a shadda on the qaf, in the past tense, referring to the lamp, meaning: it blazed. It is said: "tawaqqadati al-nar," meaning the fire blazed. Ahl al-Kufa other than Hafs read "tūqadu" with a ta' and a damma, and a fatha on the qaf lightly, referring to the glass, meaning: the fire of the glass, because glass is not kindled. The others read it with a ya' and a damma lightly, referring to the lamp. ﴿From a blessed tree, an olive tree﴾, that is: from the oil of a blessed tree, so the noun was omitted, as indicated by His saying: ﴿whose oil almost gives light﴾. By the blessed tree is meant the olive tree, which is abundant in blessing, and in which there are many benefits, because its oil is used for lamps; it is the brightest and purest of oils, it is a condiment and a fruit, and its extraction needs no press; rather, everyone can extract it. There came in a hadith: "It is a cure for piles," [[Al-Tabarani recorded it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/281), and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (2/279) and said: "My father said: this is a lie." Al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan (3/40) in the biography of Uthman ibn Salih, and he is the defect of this hadith; Ahmad ibn Salih is weak. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/100): "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahi'a, whose hadith is good, and the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih; but al-Dhahabi mentioned this hadith in the biography of Uthman from Abu Salih and quoted Abu Hatim as saying he was a liar." Ibn Hajar added its attribution to Abu Nu'aym in al-Tibb, and to al-Tha'labi. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 119; Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifa: 1/228.]] and it is a tree that bears leaves from its top to its bottom.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu al-Hasan al-Qasim ibn Bakr al-Tayalisi informed us: Abu Umayya al-Tarsusi informed us: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba informed us: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa, from 'Ata' who was in al-Sham, and he is not Ibn Abi Rabah, from Asad ibn Thabit and Abu Aslam al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Eat olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it is from a blessed tree." [[Al-Tirmidhi recorded it in the Book of Foods, chapter on what has come concerning eating olive oil (5/585–586), and said: "This is a strange hadith from this route; we only know it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa." Al-Hakim declared it sahih (2/398). Al-Darimi recorded it in al-Sunan (2/28), Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (3/497), and the author in Sharh al-Sunna (11/311).
Al-Albani said: "It has been narrated from the hadith of 'Umar, Abu Usayd, Abu Hurayra and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas..." and he cited its routes to them, then said: "The summary is that the hadith, by the combination of the route of 'Umar and the route of Abu Sa'id, rises to the level of hasan (good) by virtue of other routes, at the least. And Allah knows best." See: Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahiha: 1/354–357.]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾, that is: it is not eastern alone, so that the sun does not reach it when it sets, nor western alone, so that the sun does not reach it in the morning when it rises; rather it is exposed to the sun the whole day, the sun reaching it at its rising and at its setting, so it is both eastern and western, taking its share from both. Thus its oil is brighter. This is like saying: "So-and-so is neither black nor white," meaning he is neither purely black nor purely white, but each of the two colours is combined in him. And this pomegranate is neither sweet nor sour, meaning sweetness and sourness are combined in it. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of 'Ikrima and al-Kalbi, and of most people. Al-Suddi and a group said: its meaning is that it is not in a place of shade where the sun does not reach it, nor in a place of sunlight where the shade does not reach it; it is harmed neither by the sun nor by shade.

It was said: its meaning is that it is temperate, not in an east that harms it with heat, nor in a west that harms it with cold. It was said: its meaning is that it is Syrian, because Syria is neither eastern nor western. Al-Hasan said: this is not one of the trees of this world; had it been in this world it would have been eastern or western. Rather, it is a parable that Allah struck for His light. [[Al-Tabari mentioned these sayings, then said: "The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: it is eastern and western. He said: the meaning of the speech is: it is not eastern, upon which the sun rises in the evening and not in the morning, but the sun shines upon it and sets upon it, so it is eastern and western. We only said that is more correct as the meaning of the speech, because Allah described the oil lit in this lamp by its purity and excellence; if its tree is eastern and western, then its oil is undoubtedly better, purer and brighter." Tafsir al-Tabari: 18/142–143.]]

﴿Its oil almost﴾: its oil, ﴿gives light﴾ because of its purity, ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾, that is, before the fire reaches it. ﴿Light upon light﴾: meaning the light of the lamp upon the light of the glass. The people of knowledge differed concerning the meaning of this parable. Some of them said: this parable was struck for the light of Muhammad (ﷺ). Ibn 'Abbas said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Tell me about His saying: ﴿the likeness of His light is like a niche﴾." Ka'b said: "This is a parable Allah struck for His Prophet (ﷺ). The niche is his chest, the glass is his heart, and the lamp in it is prophethood, kindled from a blessed tree, which is the tree of prophethood, ﴿almost the light of Muhammad and his affair becomes clear to the people, even if he did not speak, that he is a prophet, just as that oil almost gives light even if no fire touched it.﴾" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (6/198) to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.]] Salim narrated from Ibn 'Umar concerning this verse, he said: "The niche is the inside of Muhammad, the glass is his heart, and the lamp is the light which Allah placed in it; ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾: neither Jewish nor Christian; ﴿kindled from a blessed tree﴾: Abraham; ﴿light upon light﴾: the heart of Abraham, and light: the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ)." [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (6/198) to al-Tabarani, Ibn 'Adi, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "The niche" is Abraham, "the glass" is Isma'il, and "the lamp" is Muhammad, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all. Allah named him "lamp" just as He named him "lantern," when He said: ﴿and as a lantern giving light﴾ [al-Ahzab: 46]. "Kindled from a blessed tree" is Abraham; He called him "blessed" because most of the prophets came from his loins. "Neither eastern nor western" means: Abraham was neither Jewish nor Christian, but was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, because the Jews pray facing the west and the Christians pray facing the east. ﴿Its oil almost gives light, even if no fire touched it﴾: the noble qualities of Muhammad (ﷺ) almost appear to the people before he received revelation. ﴿Light upon light﴾: a prophet from the offspring of a prophet, the light of Muhammad upon the light of Abraham.

Some scholars said: this parable was given for the light of the believer's heart. Abu al-Aliyah related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "This is the parable of the believer. The niche (mishkah) is himself, the glass (zujajah) is his chest, and the lamp (misbah) is what Allah has placed in him of faith and the Qur'an in his heart. It is kindled from a blessed tree, which is sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah alone. So his likeness is that of the tree around which trees have intertwined, green and luxuriant, which the sun does not touch, neither when it rises nor when it sets. Likewise the believer has guarded himself from being struck by any of the trials (fitan). He is between four qualities: if he is given, he is thankful; if he is tested, he is patient; if he judges, he is just; and if he speaks, he is truthful. 'Its oil would almost glow': that is, the heart of the believer almost recognizes the truth before it is made clear to him, because it agrees with it. 'Light upon light.'" Ubayy said: "So he moves within five lights: his speech is light, his action is light, his entering is light, his exiting is light, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is to the light." [Related by al-Tabari, 18/138; see also al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/197.]

Ibn Abbas said: This is the parable of Allah's light and guidance in the heart of the believer, just as pure oil almost glows before the fire touches it; when the fire touches it, its light increases upon its light. Likewise the heart of the believer almost acts upon guidance before knowledge comes to it; when knowledge comes to it, its guidance increases upon guidance and its light upon light. [Al-Tabari himself; al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/197.]

Al-Kalbi said: the words ﴿light upon light﴾ mean the faith of the believer and his deeds. As-Suddi said: the light of faith and the light of the Qur'an. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd [al-Tabari, 18/137] said: this is a parable of the Qur'an. The lamp is the Qur'an, and just as one is guided by a lamp, one is guided by the Qur'an. The glass is the heart of the believer, and the niche is his mouth and tongue. The blessed tree is the tree of revelation. "Its oil would almost glow": the proof of the Qur'an almost becomes clear even if it is not recited. "Light upon light": the Qur'an is a light from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His creation, together with the signs and indications He established for them before the Qur'an was revealed, so that it increased in light upon light. [See what has been previously quoted from al-Tabari in favoring that this is a parable Allah struck for the Qur'an in the hearts of the people of faith in it: p. 46.]

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: to the religion of Islam, and this is the light of insight. It was also said: it is the Qur'an. ﴿And Allah strikes parables for the people﴾: Allah makes things clear to the people, bringing them near to understanding and facilitating the paths of comprehension. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 34–35 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that make things clear﴾, of the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾, that is, a likeness of your situation to theirs, O deniers. This is a warning to them that there may befall them what befell those deniers before them, ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾, the believers who guard against shirk (association of partners with God) and the major sins.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He is the Guide of the people of the heavens and the earth; by His light they are guided to the truth, and by His guidance they are saved from misguidance. Al-Dahhak said: He is the Illuminator of the heavens and the earth. It is said: He illuminated the sky with the angels and illuminated the earth with the prophets. Mujahid said: He is the Manager of affairs in the heavens and the earth. [[Al-Tabari mentioned these three sayings, and he preferred the first, which was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.]] Ubayy ibn Ka'b, al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah said: He is the Adorner of the heavens and the earth. He adorned the sky with the sun, the moon and the stars, and He adorned the earth with the prophets, the scholars and the believers. It is also said: with plants and trees. It was also said: its meaning is that all lights are from Him, just as it is said: "So-and-so is mercy," meaning that mercy comes from him. Such a term may also be used in praise, as the poet said:

*"When 'Abd Allah travels a night from Marw,*
*Its light and its beauty have traveled from it."*

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿the likeness of His light﴾, that is, the likeness of the light of Allah Exalted in the heart of the believer, which is the light by which he is guided, as He said: "So he is upon a light from his Lord" [al-Zumar: 22]. Ibn Mas'ud used to recite: "the likeness of His light in the heart of the believer." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn 'Abbas: the likeness of His light which He gave to the believer. Some said: the pronoun refers to the believer, meaning the likeness of the light of the believer's heart. Ubayy used to recite: "the likeness of the light of one who believed in Him," and he is a servant in whose breast faith and the Qur'an have been placed. Al-Hasan and Zayd ibn Aslam said: by the light is meant the Qur'an. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak said: it is Muhammad (ﷺ). It was also said: by the light is meant obedience; He named obedience to Allah "light" and attributed these lights to Himself as an honour. ﴿Like a niche﴾, and it is the recess that has no opening; if it has an opening, it is a window (kuwwa). It was said: the mishkah is an Abyssinian word. Mujahid said: it is the lamp-stand. [[Al-Tabari said (18/140): "The most correct of the sayings concerning this is the saying of the one who said: it is a parable that Allah struck for the Qur'an in the heart of the people of faith in it. He said: the likeness of the light of Allah, by which He illuminated for His servants the path of right guidance which He sent down to them, so they believed in it and affirmed what is in it, in the hearts of the believers, is like a niche, which is the pillar of the lamp in which is the wick, and that is the counterpart of the recess in the walls that has no opening. That is a likeness of the Qur'an. He says: the Qur'an that is in the heart of the believer, whose heart Allah has illuminated, in his breast; then He likened the breast in its purity from disbelief in Allah and doubt concerning Him, and its being illuminated by the light of the Qur'an, and its being lit by the clear verses of its Lord and its admonitions in it, to a bright star, saying: the glass. That is the breast of the believer, in which is his heart, as if it were a bright star."]] ﴿in it is a lamp﴾, that is, a lantern. Its root is from light, and from it comes "ṣubḥ" (dawn). Its meaning: like a lamp in a niche. ﴿The lamp is in a glass﴾, meaning the lamp-stand. Al-Zajjaj said: he mentioned the glass only because the light and the brightness of the fire within it are clearer than anything else, and its light increases through the glass. Then He described the glass, saying: ﴿the glass is as if it were a glittering star﴾. Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read "durri'in" with a kasra on the dal and the hamza. Hamzah and Abu Bakr read it with a damma on the dal and the hamza. As for the one who reads it with a kasra on the dal, it is fa'il (the pattern) from al-dar', which means "pushing away," because the star pushes away the devils from the sky. He likened it to the state of being pushed, because in that state it is brighter and more luminous. It is also said: it is from dara'a al-kawkab, when the star moves away, contracting, so its light doubles at that time. It was also said: "durri" means rising, as it is said: daraa al-najm when the star rose and ascended. It is also said: daraa 'alayna fulan, meaning he appeared and became visible. As for raising the dal together with the hamza as Hamzah read, most grammarians said: it is a lahn (a grammatical error; a solecism), because there is no fu'ayl pattern with a damma on the fa' and a kasra on the 'ayn in the speech of the Arabs.

Abu 'Ubayda said: I see a valid form for it, namely that it is durru'un, on the pattern fu'ul from daraat, like subbuh and quddus, and they found the accumulation of dammas heavy, so they changed some of them to a kasra, as they said: 'itiyyan, which is fu'ul from 'atawtu. The others read ﴿durriyyun﴾ with a damma on the dal and a shadda on the ya without a hamza, meaning: very bright, attributed to the pearl (durr) for its purity and beauty. Although the star has more light than a pearl, it surpasses the stars in its brightness, just as a pearl surpasses all other grains. It was also said: the "durri" star is one of the five great planets, which are Saturn, Mars, Jupiter, Venus and Mercury. It was said: He likened it to a star and did not liken it to the sun and the moon, because the sun and the moon are subject to eclipse, while the stars are not subject to eclipse.

﴿Yūqadu﴾: Abu Ja'far, Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read "tawaqqada" with a ta' and its vowelling, with a fatha on the waw and the dal, and a shadda on the qaf, in the past tense, referring to the lamp, meaning: it blazed. It is said: "tawaqqadati al-nar," meaning the fire blazed. Ahl al-Kufa other than Hafs read "tūqadu" with a ta' and a damma, and a fatha on the qaf lightly, referring to the glass, meaning: the fire of the glass, because glass is not kindled. The others read it with a ya' and a damma lightly, referring to the lamp. ﴿From a blessed tree, an olive tree﴾, that is: from the oil of a blessed tree, so the noun was omitted, as indicated by His saying: ﴿whose oil almost gives light﴾. By the blessed tree is meant the olive tree, which is abundant in blessing, and in which there are many benefits, because its oil is used for lamps; it is the brightest and purest of oils, it is a condiment and a fruit, and its extraction needs no press; rather, everyone can extract it. There came in a hadith: "It is a cure for piles," [[Al-Tabarani recorded it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (17/281), and Ibn Abi Hatim in al-'Ilal (2/279) and said: "My father said: this is a lie." Al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan (3/40) in the biography of Uthman ibn Salih, and he is the defect of this hadith; Ahmad ibn Salih is weak. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/100): "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Ibn Lahi'a, whose hadith is good, and the rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih; but al-Dhahabi mentioned this hadith in the biography of Uthman from Abu Salih and quoted Abu Hatim as saying he was a liar." Ibn Hajar added its attribution to Abu Nu'aym in al-Tibb, and to al-Tha'labi. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 119; Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifa: 1/228.]] and it is a tree that bears leaves from its top to its bottom.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu al-Hasan al-Qasim ibn Bakr al-Tayalisi informed us: Abu Umayya al-Tarsusi informed us: Qabisa ibn 'Uqba informed us: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa, from 'Ata' who was in al-Sham, and he is not Ibn Abi Rabah, from Asad ibn Thabit and Abu Aslam al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Eat olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it is from a blessed tree." [[Al-Tirmidhi recorded it in the Book of Foods, chapter on what has come concerning eating olive oil (5/585–586), and said: "This is a strange hadith from this route; we only know it from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Isa." Al-Hakim declared it sahih (2/398). Al-Darimi recorded it in al-Sunan (2/28), Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (3/497), and the author in Sharh al-Sunna (11/311).
Al-Albani said: "It has been narrated from the hadith of 'Umar, Abu Usayd, Abu Hurayra and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas..." and he cited its routes to them, then said: "The summary is that the hadith, by the combination of the route of 'Umar and the route of Abu Sa'id, rises to the level of hasan (good) by virtue of other routes, at the least. And Allah knows best." See: Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahiha: 1/354–357.]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾, that is: it is not eastern alone, so that the sun does not reach it when it sets, nor western alone, so that the sun does not reach it in the morning when it rises; rather it is exposed to the sun the whole day, the sun reaching it at its rising and at its setting, so it is both eastern and western, taking its share from both. Thus its oil is brighter. This is like saying: "So-and-so is neither black nor white," meaning he is neither purely black nor purely white, but each of the two colours is combined in him. And this pomegranate is neither sweet nor sour, meaning sweetness and sourness are combined in it. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of 'Ikrima and al-Kalbi, and of most people. Al-Suddi and a group said: its meaning is that it is not in a place of shade where the sun does not reach it, nor in a place of sunlight where the shade does not reach it; it is harmed neither by the sun nor by shade.

It was said: its meaning is that it is temperate, not in an east that harms it with heat, nor in a west that harms it with cold. It was said: its meaning is that it is Syrian, because Syria is neither eastern nor western. Al-Hasan said: this is not one of the trees of this world; had it been in this world it would have been eastern or western. Rather, it is a parable that Allah struck for His light. [[Al-Tabari mentioned these sayings, then said: "The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: it is eastern and western. He said: the meaning of the speech is: it is not eastern, upon which the sun rises in the evening and not in the morning, but the sun shines upon it and sets upon it, so it is eastern and western. We only said that is more correct as the meaning of the speech, because Allah described the oil lit in this lamp by its purity and excellence; if its tree is eastern and western, then its oil is undoubtedly better, purer and brighter." Tafsir al-Tabari: 18/142–143.]]

﴿Its oil almost﴾: its oil, ﴿gives light﴾ because of its purity, ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾, that is, before the fire reaches it. ﴿Light upon light﴾: meaning the light of the lamp upon the light of the glass. The people of knowledge differed concerning the meaning of this parable. Some of them said: this parable was struck for the light of Muhammad (ﷺ). Ibn 'Abbas said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Tell me about His saying: ﴿the likeness of His light is like a niche﴾." Ka'b said: "This is a parable Allah struck for His Prophet (ﷺ). The niche is his chest, the glass is his heart, and the lamp in it is prophethood, kindled from a blessed tree, which is the tree of prophethood, ﴿almost the light of Muhammad and his affair becomes clear to the people, even if he did not speak, that he is a prophet, just as that oil almost gives light even if no fire touched it.﴾" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (6/198) to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh.]] Salim narrated from Ibn 'Umar concerning this verse, he said: "The niche is the inside of Muhammad, the glass is his heart, and the lamp is the light which Allah placed in it; ﴿neither eastern nor western﴾: neither Jewish nor Christian; ﴿kindled from a blessed tree﴾: Abraham; ﴿light upon light﴾: the heart of Abraham, and light: the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ)." [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (6/198) to al-Tabarani, Ibn 'Adi, Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn 'Asakir.]]

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "The niche" is Abraham, "the glass" is Isma'il, and "the lamp" is Muhammad, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all. Allah named him "lamp" just as He named him "lantern," when He said: ﴿and as a lantern giving light﴾ [al-Ahzab: 46]. "Kindled from a blessed tree" is Abraham; He called him "blessed" because most of the prophets came from his loins. "Neither eastern nor western" means: Abraham was neither Jewish nor Christian, but was a ḥanīf, a Muslim, because the Jews pray facing the west and the Christians pray facing the east. ﴿Its oil almost gives light, even if no fire touched it﴾: the noble qualities of Muhammad (ﷺ) almost appear to the people before he received revelation. ﴿Light upon light﴾: a prophet from the offspring of a prophet, the light of Muhammad upon the light of Abraham.

Some scholars said: this parable was given for the light of the believer's heart. Abu al-Aliyah related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "This is the parable of the believer. The niche (mishkah) is himself, the glass (zujajah) is his chest, and the lamp (misbah) is what Allah has placed in him of faith and the Qur'an in his heart. It is kindled from a blessed tree, which is sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah alone. So his likeness is that of the tree around which trees have intertwined, green and luxuriant, which the sun does not touch, neither when it rises nor when it sets. Likewise the believer has guarded himself from being struck by any of the trials (fitan). He is between four qualities: if he is given, he is thankful; if he is tested, he is patient; if he judges, he is just; and if he speaks, he is truthful. 'Its oil would almost glow': that is, the heart of the believer almost recognizes the truth before it is made clear to him, because it agrees with it. 'Light upon light.'" Ubayy said: "So he moves within five lights: his speech is light, his action is light, his entering is light, his exiting is light, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is to the light." [Related by al-Tabari, 18/138; see also al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/197.]

Ibn Abbas said: This is the parable of Allah's light and guidance in the heart of the believer, just as pure oil almost glows before the fire touches it; when the fire touches it, its light increases upon its light. Likewise the heart of the believer almost acts upon guidance before knowledge comes to it; when knowledge comes to it, its guidance increases upon guidance and its light upon light. [Al-Tabari himself; al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/197.]

Al-Kalbi said: the words ﴿light upon light﴾ mean the faith of the believer and his deeds. As-Suddi said: the light of faith and the light of the Qur'an. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd [al-Tabari, 18/137] said: this is a parable of the Qur'an. The lamp is the Qur'an, and just as one is guided by a lamp, one is guided by the Qur'an. The glass is the heart of the believer, and the niche is his mouth and tongue. The blessed tree is the tree of revelation. "Its oil would almost glow": the proof of the Qur'an almost becomes clear even if it is not recited. "Light upon light": the Qur'an is a light from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to His creation, together with the signs and indications He established for them before the Qur'an was revealed, so that it increased in light upon light. [See what has been previously quoted from al-Tabari in favoring that this is a parable Allah struck for the Qur'an in the hearts of the people of faith in it: p. 46.]

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: to the religion of Islam, and this is the light of insight. It was also said: it is the Qur'an. ﴿And Allah strikes parables for the people﴾: Allah makes things clear to the people, bringing them near to understanding and facilitating the paths of comprehension. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ اللَّهُ﴾ أَيْ: ذَلِكَ الْمِصْبَاحُ فِي بُيُوتٍ. وَقِيلَ: يُوقَدُ فِي بُيُوتٍ، وَالْبُيُوتُ: هِيَ الْمَسَاجِدُ، قَالَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا أَنَّهُ قَالَ: "الْمَسَاجِدُ بُيُوتُ اللَّهِ فِي الْأَرْضِ، وهي تضيء ٤١/ب لِأَهْلِ السَّمَاءِ كَمَا تُضِيءُ النُّجُومُ لِأَهْلِ الْأَرْضِ".

وَرَوَى صَالِحُ بْنُ حَيَّانَ عَنِ ابْنِ بُرَيْدَةَ فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: "فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ اللَّهُ"، قَالَ: إِنَّمَا هِيَ أَرْبَعَةُ مَسَاجِدَ لَمْ يَبْنِهَا إِلَّا نَبِيٌّ: الْكَعْبَةُ بَنَاهَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ فَجَعَلَاهَا قِبْلَةً، وَبَيْتُ الْمَقْدِسِ بَنَاهُ دَاوُدُ وَسُلَيْمَانُ، وَمَسْجِدُ الْمَدِينَةِ بَنَاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ)، وَمَسْجِدُ قُبَاءٍ أُسِّسَ عَلَى التَّقْوَى بَنَاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) [[انظر: الدر المنثور: ٦ / ٢٠٣.]]

قَوْلُهُ: ﴿أَنْ تُرْفَعَ﴾ قَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: أَنْ تُبْنَى، نَظِيرُهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ﴾ [البقرة: ١٢٧]، قَالَ الْحَسَنُ: أَيْ تُعَظَّمَ، أَيْ لَا يُذْكَرَ فِيهِ الْخَنَا مِنَ الْقَوْلِ.

﴿وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ﴾ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: يُتْلَى فِيهَا كِتَابُهُ. ﴿يُسَبِّحُ﴾ قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَامِرٍ وَأَبُو بَكْرٍ "يُسَبَّحُ" بِفَتْحِ الْبَاءِ عَلَى غَيْرِ تَسْمِيَةِ الْفَاعِلِ، وَالْوَقْفُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْقِرَاءَةِ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ: "وَالْآصَالِ"، وَقَرَأَ الْآخَرُونَ بِكَسْرِ الْبَاءِ، جَعَلُوا التَّسْبِيحَ فِعْلًا لِلرِّجَالِ. ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ﴾ أَيْ: يُصَلِّي، ﴿لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ﴾ أَيْ: بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ. قَالَ أَهْلُ التَّفْسِيرِ (tafsir: exegesis): أَرَادَ بِهِ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْمَفْرُوضَاتِ. فَالَّتِي تُؤَدَّى بِالْغَدَاةِ صَلَاةُ الصُّبْحِ، وَالَّتِي تُؤَدَّى بِالْآصَالِ صَلَاةُ الظُّهْرِ وَالْعَصْرِ وَالْعِشَاءَيْنِ، لِأَنَّ اسْمَ الْأَصِيلِ يَجْمَعُهُمَا. وَقِيلَ: أَرَادَ بِهِ صَلَاةَ الصُّبْحِ وَالْعَصْرِ.

أَخْبَرَنَا الْإِمَامُ أَبُو عَلِيٍّ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْقَاضِي، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو بَكْرٍ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ الْحِيرِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَعْقِلٍ الْمَيْدَانِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ رَجَاءٍ، أَخْبَرَنَا هَمَّامُ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ، أَنَّ أَبَا بَكْرِ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) قَالَ: "مَنْ صَلَّى الْبَرْدَيْنِ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ" [[أخرجه البخاري في المواقيت، باب فضل صلاة الفجر: ٢ / ٥٢، ومسلم في المساجد، باب فضل صلاتي الصبح والعصر، برقم (٦٣٥): ١ / ٤٤٠، والمصنف في شرح السنة: ٢ / ٢٢٧.]]. وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا قَالَ: التَّسْبِيحُ بِالْغُدُوِّ صَلَاةُ الضُّحَى [[عزاه السيوطي في "الدر": (٦ / ٢٠٦) لابن أبي شيبة والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان.]]

أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَاحِدِ الْمَلِيحِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو مَنْصُورٍ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ السَّمْعَانِ، أَخْبَرَنَا أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ الرَّيَّانِيُّ، أَخْبَرَنَا حُمَيْدُ بْنُ زَنْجَوَيْهِ، أَخْبَرَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ يُوسُفَ، أَخْبَرَنَا الْهَيْثَمُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ، أَخْبَرَنِي يَحْيَى بْنُ الْحَارِثِ، عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، عَنْ أَبِي أُمَامَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): "مَنْ مَشَى إِلَى صَلَاةٍ مَكْتُوبَةٍ وَهُوَ مُتَطَهِّرٌ فَأَجْرُهُ كَأَجْرِ الْحَاجِّ الْمُحْرِمِ، وَمَنْ مَشَى إِلَى تَسْبِيحِ الضُّحَى لَا يَنْصِبُهُ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ فَأَجْرُهُ كَأَجْرِ الْمُعْتَمِرِ، وَصَلَاةٌ عَلَى أَثَرِ صَلَاةٍ لَا لَغْوَ بَيْنَهُمَا كِتَابٌ فِي عِلِّيِّينَ" [[أخرجه أبو داود في الصلاة، باب ما جاء في فضل المشي إلى الصلاة: ١ / ٢٩٤. قال المنذري: "القاسم بن عبد الرحمن فيه مقال". والإمام أحمد: ٥ / ٢٦٨، والبيهقي في السنن: ٣ / ٤٩، والطبراني في الكبير: ٨ / ١٥٠، ٢٠٧، والمصنف في شرح السنة: ٢ / ٣٥٧، وانظر: نصب الراية: ٣ / ١٥١.]]

﴿Men﴾. It is said that the men are singled out for mention in these mosques because there is no Friday prayer (Jumu'ah) or congregational prayer in the mosque obligatory upon women. ﴿Do not distract﴾ means do not occupy. ﴿Trade﴾: it is said that trade is singled out for mention because it is the greatest thing with which a person occupies himself to the neglect of prayer and acts of obedience. By "trade" he means buying, although the term "trade" applies to both buying and selling, because he mentions selling after it, as in His saying: "And when they see a trade" [al-Jumu'ah: 11], meaning buying. Al-Farra' said: "Trade" belongs to the importers of goods and the sellers, which is what a man sells with his own hands. His saying: ﴿nor selling, from remembrance of Allah﴾ means from attending the mosques to establish the prayer. ﴿And establishing﴾ means for the establishment of, ﴿prayer﴾. He omitted the ha' (the feminine suffix) and meant performing it at its proper time, because whoever delays the prayer beyond its time is not among those who establish the prayer. He repeated mention of establishing the prayer, although what is meant by "the remembrance of Allah" is the five daily prayers, because by "establishing the prayer" he meant observing its appointed times.

Salim reported from Ibn Umar that he was in the marketplace when the prayer was called, and the people rose, closed their shops, and entered the mosque. Ibn Umar said: "It was concerning them that this was revealed: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor selling distracts from the remembrance of Allah and establishing the prayer﴾" [[Narrated by al-Tabari (18/146), Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Abi Hatim. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/207.]]

﴿And giving zakat﴾, the obligatory alms (zakat). Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: When the time for paying zakat arrives, they do not withhold it. It is also said: it refers to righteous deeds in general.

﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾. It is said: the hearts will turn away from what they were upon in the world of polytheism and disbelief, and the eyes will be opened from their coverings. It is also said: the hearts will turn between fear and hope, fearing destruction and hoping for salvation. The turning of the eyes is from its terror, meaning in which direction they will be taken, to the right or to the left, and from where they will be given their books, whether from the right side, the left side, or from the direction of the left. That is the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: the hearts will turn within the chest, rising up to the throat so that they neither descend nor come out. The turning of the gaze is its fixed stare from the awfulness and severity of the matter.

﴿So that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did﴾. He means: they were occupied with the remembrance of Allah, establishing the prayer, and giving zakat, so that Allah may reward them with the best of what they did, meaning with the best of what they did. He means: He rewards them for their good deeds, and He does not reward them for the bad aspects of their deeds. ﴿And increase them from His bounty﴾, that is, what they did not deserve by their deeds. ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾.
