Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 39–40:

﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain﴾ "As-sarab" (the mirage) is the shimmer seen at midday in the heat of intense summer in the deserts; it resembles flowing water upon the ground, so that whoever sees it thinks it is water. When he comes near it, it dissipates, and he sees nothing. "Al-al" is what rises up from the ground, a shimmer seen between the sky and the earth in the mornings, like a sheet in which figures are raised; in it the small appears large and the short appears tall. "Ar-raqraq" occurs in the evenings, and it is what quivers from the mirage, that is, it comes and goes. "Al-qi'ah" is the plural of "al-qa'," which is the flat, wide expanse of the earth, and in it the mirage occurs. ﴿The thirsty one thinks it to be water﴾, that is, the thirsty one imagines it, ﴿until, when he comes to it﴾, that is, he comes to what he had thought was water. It is also said: he comes to the place of the mirage. ﴿He finds it to be nothing﴾, as he had estimated and supposed. Likewise the disbeliever thinks that his deed will benefit him; but when the Angel of Death comes to him and he has need of his deed, he finds that his deed has not enriched him in the least, nor benefited him.

﴿And he finds Allah with him﴾, that is, with his deed; that is, he finds Allah lying in wait. It is also said: he has come before Allah. ﴿So He pays him his account in full﴾, that is, the recompense for his deed. ﴿And Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾

﴿Or [they are] like darknesses﴾. This is another parable which Allah has struck for the deeds of the disbelievers. He says: the likeness of their deeds, owing to their corruption and their ignorance in them, is like darknesses ﴿in a deep sea﴾, which is the profound, abundant in water; and the "lujjat al-bahr" is its main body. ﴿Covered by waves﴾, that is, overspread. ﴿Above it waves, piled upon one another﴾, ﴿above it clouds﴾ 42/a. Ibn Kathir, according to the narration of al-Qawwas, read "sahabun" with a damma and tanwin, ﴿darknesses﴾ in the genitive as a substitute for his saying "or like darknesses." Abu al-Hasan al-Burri narrated from him: "sahabu, zulumatin" with an idafa. The others read "sahabun zulumatun," both with a damma and tanwin, so that the complete sentence ends at his saying "sahabun," and then he begins: ﴿darknesses, some above others﴾: the darkness of the clouds, the darkness of the waves, and the darkness of the sea, some above others; that is, the darkness of the waves upon the darkness of the sea, the darkness of the waves above the waves, and the darkness of the clouds upon the darkness of the waves. By the darknesses he means the deeds of the disbeliever, by the deep sea his heart, by the waves what covers his heart of ignorance, doubt and bewilderment, and by the clouds the sealing and stamping upon his heart.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: concerning this verse, the disbeliever moves about in five kinds of darkness: his speech is darkness, his deed is darkness, his entrance is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his destination is toward the darknesses on the Day of Resurrection, toward the Fire. [[al-Tabari: 18/151.]]

﴿If he brings out his hand﴾, meaning the one looking, ﴿he is not near to seeing it﴾, meaning he is not close to seeing it because of the intensity of the darkness. Al-Farra' said: "yakad" is a filler; that is, he did not see it, [al-Mubarrad said: meaning he did not see it] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] except after great effort, as one says: "I could hardly see you in the darkness," though he did see him, but only after despair and difficulty. It is also said: the meaning is that he came close to seeing it but did not see it, as one says: "The ostrich almost flew."

﴿And whomever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: whomever Allah does not grant religion and faith, for him there is no religion. It is also said: whomever Allah does not guide, for him there is no faith, and no one can guide him. Muqatil said: this verse was revealed concerning Utbah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Umayyah, who used to seek religion in the Jahiliyyah and would wear woolen garments; but when Islam came, he disbelieved. Most scholars hold that it is general concerning all disbelievers. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 6/460.]]

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-Nur, verses 41–43**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah is glorified by whoever is in the heavens and the earth, and by the birds spreading their wings in flight?﴾ *Saffat* means spreading their wings in the air. It is said that He singled out birds for mention from among the animals because they are between the sky and the earth, so they are excluded from the ruling concerning those in the heavens and the earth. ﴿Each knows its prayer and its glorification.﴾ Mujahid said: prayer is for the children of Adam, and glorification is for the rest of creation. It is also said that the beating of the wings is the bird's prayer, and its sound is its glorification.

His saying, ﴿Each knows﴾, means: every one who prays and glorifies, Allah knows its prayer and its glorification. It is also said that its meaning is: every one of them that prays and glorifies knows its own prayer and glorification. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the final return.﴾

﴿Have you not seen that Allah drives﴾ means: He drives by His command, ﴿clouds﴾ to wherever He wills. ﴿Then He joins them together﴾ means: He gathers the scattered pieces of cloud, some to others. ﴿Then He makes them into a heap﴾ means: piled up, some on top of others. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾, meaning the rainfall, ﴿emerging from within it﴾, meaning from its midst. *Khilal* is the plural of *khalal*, like *jibal* is the plural of *jabal*.

﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail in it﴾ means: He sends down hail. The word *min* (in *min jibal*) is a supplementary particle (*silah*). It is also said that the meaning is: He sends down from the sky, from mountains, that is, an amount of hail as great as mountains. The *min* in His saying *min jibal* is supplementary, meaning: He sends down from the sky mountains of hail. It is also said that the meaning is: He sends down from mountains in the sky, those mountains being of hail. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: Allah, exalted is He, informed that in the sky there are mountains of hail. The object of the verb "sends down" is omitted, its implied sense being: "He sends down from the sky, from mountains in which there is hail," so the object is dispensed with because its meaning is indicated.

The grammarians said: Allah, exalted is He, mentioned *min* three times in this verse. His saying *min al-sama'* ("from the sky") indicates the starting point (*ibtida' al-ghayah*), since the descent begins from the sky. His saying *min jibal* ("from mountains") indicates partitive (*tab'id*), since what Allah sends down is some of those mountains that are in the sky. His saying *min barad* ("of hail") indicates specification of kind (*tajnis*), since those mountains are of the kind of hail.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verses 45–47:**

His, may He be exalted and glorified, saying: ﴿And Allah created every creature (dabbah)﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "khaliq kulli" (creator of every) with the genitive construction (idafah). The others recited "khalaqa kulla" as a finite verb. ﴿From water﴾ means: from a drop of semen (nutfah). By it He intended every living creature that is observed in this world. The angels and the jinn are not included, because we do not observe them. It was also said: the origin of all creation is water. Allah, exalted is He, created water, then made part of it wind, from which He created the angels; part of it fire, from which He created the jinn; and part of it clay, from which He created Adam. ﴿Among them are those that walk on their bellies﴾, such as snakes, fish and worms. ﴿And among them are those that walk on two legs﴾, such as the children of Adam and birds. ﴿And among them are those that walk on four﴾, such as cattle and beasts of prey. Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And they are not believers.﴾ This verse was revealed concerning Bishr the hypocrite. He had a dispute with a Jewish man over a piece of land. The Jew said, "Let us take our case to Muhammad ﷺ." The hypocrite said, "Let us take it to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, for Muhammad is unjust toward us." So Allah revealed this verse. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 48–53:

And He said: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them﴾ — the Messenger (by the judgment of Allah) — ﴿behold, a party of them turn away﴾, i.e., from the judgment. It was also said: from responding.

﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly﴾ — obedient, submissive to his judgment. That is: when the right is theirs against others, they hasten to his judgment, because of their confidence that just as he judges against them with the truth, he also judges in their favor with the truth.

﴿Is there a disease in their hearts, or do they have doubt?﴾ — i.e., they doubt. This is a question of reproach and censure, meaning: they are indeed like this. ﴿Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them?﴾ — i.e., by injustice. ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ — wronging themselves by their turning away from the truth.

﴿The saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger﴾ — to the Book of Allah and His Messenger — ﴿that he may judge between them﴾: this is not in the form of a report, but rather the teaching of the etiquette of the Sharia, in the sense that the believers ought to be such. The accusative of "qawl" (saying) is due to its being the predicate, and its subject is in His words, Exalted is He: ﴿that they say, "We hear and we obey"﴾, i.e., we hear the call and obey by responding.

﴿And it is those who are the successful﴾. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ — Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: in what pleases him and what displeases him. ﴿And fears Allah﴾ — for the sins he has committed.

﴿And keeps his duty to Him﴾ — in what follows, ﴿those are the victorious﴾, the saved. Abu 'Amr and Abu Bakr read "yattqih" with the ha' sukun (yattaqhi → "yattaqhi" with a silent ha'), while Abu Ja'far, Ya'qub and Qalun pronounce it with a brief vowel (ikhtilas), as in its parallels, and the rest pronounce it with a full kasra (ishba'). Hafs read "yattaqhu" with sukun on the qaf and ikhtilas of the ha'. This dialect: when the yā' drops for jazm (apocope), they make the letter before it sukun, saying: lam ashtar ṭa'aman (I did not buy food), with sukun on the ra'.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths﴾ — the utmost of an oath is to swear by Allah, and there is no oath above swearing by Allah. ﴿If you command them, they will surely go forth﴾. This is because the hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Wherever you are, we will be with you; if you go forth, we will go forth, and if you stay, we will stay, and if you command us to fight, we will fight." So Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿"Do not swear; [your] obedience is known"﴾ — i.e., this is obedience by word and tongue only, without belief. "Known" means: a matter known about you, that you lie and say what you do not do. This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid, may Allah be pleased with him. It was also said: its meaning is: "obedience that is known" with sincere intention is better and more excellent than an oath on the tongue which the deed does not match. Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: let there be among you an obedience that is known.

﴿Indeed Allah is Aware of what you do﴾.

A man among them said: "Will there not come a day upon us when we will be safe and lay down our weapons?" It was also said: ﴿as He granted succession to those before them﴾, meaning the Children of Israel, when He destroyed the tyrants in Egypt and Syria and made them heirs to their land and their dwellings. ﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them﴾, meaning: which He chose. The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 24, verse 58:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾, and the rest of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a young man from the Ansar called Mudlij ibn 'Amr to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, at midday to summon him. He entered and saw 'Umar in a state that 'Umar disliked to be seen in, so Allah revealed this verse. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul (Occasions of Revelation) by al-Wahidi, p. (380); al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (120).]]

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Marthad. She had an adult servant boy who entered upon her at a time she disliked. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Our servants and our boys enter upon us in a state we dislike." So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (6/217) to Ibn Abi Hatim, and mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. (380). See also: al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (120), and Ibn Kathir: 3/304.]] "O you who believe, let them ask your permission."

"Liyastadhinkum" (let them ask your permission): the lam is the lam of command (lam al-amr).

﴿Those whom your right hands possess﴾ means: the male and female slaves. ﴿And those among you who have not reached puberty﴾ means: among the free. The intended ones are not the young children who have not yet become aware of women's private matters, but those who understand matters concerning women yet have not reached puberty.

﴿Three times﴾, meaning: they must ask permission at three times: ﴿before the prayer of dawn, and when you take off your clothes at midday﴾, meaning the time of rest (al-maqil), ﴿and after the prayer of 'isha'﴾. He specified these times because they are the hours of privacy and of removing clothes, when a person may reveal what he does not wish anyone to see. He commanded the slaves and the children to ask permission at these times. As for others, they must ask permission at all times.

﴿Three times of privacy (awrat) for you﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read "thalatha" with a fatha on the tha', in apposition to "thalatha marrat" (three times). The others read it with a damma, meaning: these times are three times of privacy for you. These times were called awrat (times of privacy) because a person removes his clothes during them and his private parts become exposed.

﴿There is no sin upon you﴾, ﴿nor upon them﴾, meaning the slaves, the servants and the children, ﴿for [the one who enters] without permission﴾ upon you, ﴿after these [three times]﴾, meaning after these three times, ﴿for they constantly go around among you﴾, meaning the slaves and servants go around among you, moving about, entering and leaving for their tasks without permission, ﴿some of you attending upon others﴾, meaning they circulate. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the signs, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾.

The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse. One group said it is mansukh (abrogated, a concept of naskh, abrogation). [[This was reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Qurtubi also reported it from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, though that contradicts the report from him. See: Zad al-Masir: 6/62; al-Qurtubi: 12/302.]]

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The people did not have curtains or canopies (hijal; in al-Durr and al-Qurtubi it is "hijal", plural of "hajalah", a tent-like chamber covered with cloth and having large buttons). So the servants and the female slaves would enter, and they might see from them what they did not like, so they were commanded to ask permission. Then Allah expanded provision, people adopted curtains, and He saw that this made asking permission unnecessary. [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/219. Al-Qurtubi said (12/303): "This is a good report, and it refutes the view of Sa'id and Ibn Jubayr, for it contains no evidence that the verse was abrogated, but rather that it was for a certain situation which then ceased. If such a situation returns, its ruling remains in force as it was. Indeed its ruling still holds today in many dwellings of the Muslims in the deserts, the open countryside and similar places."]]

Another group held that it is not abrogated. Sufyan narrated from Musa ibn Abi 'A'isha, who said: I asked al-Sha'bi about this verse, "Let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission": "Is it abrogated?" He said: "No, by Allah." I said: "People do not act upon it." He said: "Allah is the One sought for help." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/162-163, and attributed by al-Suyuti: 6/319 to al-Firyabi.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said regarding this verse: "Some people say it was abrogated. By Allah, it was not abrogated, but it is among the matters the people have been negligent about." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 18/163.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 59:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾, i.e., the wet dream (al-ihtilam), meaning the free ones who have reached it, ﴿then let them ask permission﴾, i.e., they shall ask permission at all times before entering upon you, ﴿just as those before them asked permission﴾, the free and the adults.

It is also said: it refers to those who were with Abraham, Moses and Jesus.

﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses﴾, i.e., His indications. It is also said: His rulings. ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the affairs of His creation, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He has arranged for them. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: a man asks permission to enter upon his mother, for this verse was revealed concerning that [[al-Tabari: 18/165.]]. Hudhayfah was asked: Does a man need to ask permission to enter upon his mother? He said: Yes, for if he does not, he may see from her what he would dislike [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 4/398, which contains other reports.]].

And He said: 'greet one another,' meaning, some of you upon others. So it is known, since He did not restrict this to some houses over others, that it refers to all of them, mosques and non-mosques alike. The meaning of His words 'greet one another' is similar to His words: 'and do not kill yourselves.'" See also al-Qurtubi (12/318).]]

﴿A greeting from Allah, blessed and good﴾. The word ﴿greeting﴾ (taḥiyyah) is in the accusative as a masdar (verbal noun, a noun derived from the verb with the same meaning), meaning: "you greet yourselves with a greeting." ﴿Blessed and good﴾. Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "good and beautiful." It is also said that blessing and goodness are mentioned here because of the reward and recompense it carries.

﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you the verses, that you may understand.﴾

The Almighty said: ﴿The believers are only those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾, meaning: with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿on a matter that gathers them together﴾, such as a battle that has arisen, or prayer, or Friday prayer (jumu'ah), or a festival ('id), or congregation (jama'ah), or consultation about a matter that has occurred. ﴿They do not depart﴾ means they do not disperse from him; they do not leave what they have gathered for, ﴿until they seek his permission﴾. The commentators said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ascended the pulpit on Friday and a man wished to leave the mosque for a need or an excuse, he would not leave until he stood opposite the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) where he could see him, so that he would know that he had only stood to ask permission, and he would give permission to whomever he wished among them. Mujahid said: The permission of the imam (leader) on Friday is that he gestures with his hand. [[Zad al-Masir: 6/67-68.]]

The people of knowledge said: Likewise, every matter on which the Muslims gather with the imam, they do not oppose him and do not withdraw from it except with his permission. When one seeks permission, the imam may grant it if he wishes, or refrain from granting it if he wishes. This applies when there is no cause preventing him from remaining. If a cause arises that prevents him from remaining, such as when a woman among them has her menstruation, or a man becomes ritually impure (junub), or an illness afflicts him, then he does not need to seek permission.

﴿Indeed, those who seek your permission are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger. So when they seek your permission for some of their affairs﴾, meaning: for some matter of theirs, ﴿give permission to whomever of them you wish﴾ to leave, meaning: if you wish, give permission, and if you wish, do not give permission. ﴿And ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 63:

﴿Do not make the summoning of the Messenger among you like the summoning of some of you by others.﴾ Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: It means, "Beware of the Messenger's supplication against you if you anger him, for his supplication necessarily brings down calamity upon you, unlike the supplication of others."[[See: al-Tabari 17/177.]] Mujahid and Qatadah said: Do not call him by his name as some of you call others, "O Muhammad, O Abd Allah," but rather honour him and exalt him, and say, "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah," in gentleness and humility.[[This is also narrated from Ibn Abbas. See: al-Tabari 17/177; al-Durr al-Manthur 6/230. Ibn Kathir related both views in his tafsir, 3/308. al-Tabari preferred the first saying of Ibn Abbas, because what precedes this is a prohibition from Allah to the believers against turning away from him in a matter that unites them all and that he dislikes, and what follows it is a warning to those who depart without his permission. So what lies between them, namely a warning that his anger might compel him to supplicate against them, is more fitting than being a command to them to honour and revere him with speech and supplication, a matter not previously mentioned.]]

﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves﴾, i.e., who go out, some of them covering others and slipping away in fear. "Liwadha" is the verbal noun of lawadha, yulawidhu, mulawadhatan, and liwadhan.

It was said: This occurred during the digging of the trench, when the hypocrites would withdraw from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in secret. Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Liwadhan" means that some of them take refuge behind others. That was because the hypocrites found it burdensome to remain in the mosque on Friday and to listen to the sermon of the Prophet ﷺ, so they would seek cover behind some of his companions and leave the mosque secretly. The meaning of His words ﴿Allah already knows﴾ is a threat of recompense.

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾, i.e., his command; "an" is redundant (silah). It was said: its meaning is that they turn away from his command and depart from him without his permission.

﴿Lest a trial befall them﴾, i.e., lest a trial befall them. Mujahid said: a calamity in this world. ﴿Or a painful punishment strike them﴾, a painful, grievous punishment in the Hereafter. It was said: a painful punishment that comes swiftly in this world.

Then He magnified Himself, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 24, verse 64:

﴿Indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, as a kingdom and as slaves. ﴿He certainly knows your condition﴾, that in which you are, of faith and hypocrisy; i.e., He knows it. "Qad" here is a superfluous particle (ṣila). ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and He will inform them of what they did﴾, of good and evil. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Tawba narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Ansari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami informed us, Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from A'isha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not let women reside in upper chambers, do not teach them writing, but teach them spinning and Surat al-Nur." [[Narrated by al-Hakim, 2/396, who said: "This hadith has a sound chain of transmission, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "Rather it is fabricated, and its flaw is Abd al-Wahhab; Abu Hatim said: he is a liar." al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/93): "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and in its chain is Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami; al-Daraqutni said: he is a liar." Ibn al-Jawzi also mentioned it in al-Ilal al-Mutanahiya. al-Suyuti also attributed it to al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman and to Ibn Mardawayh; see al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/124.]]
